brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether kinesiology taping or self-mobilization better reduces neck pain in adults who use electronic devices for long periods each day. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does kinesiology taping or self-mobilization lead to greater reduction in neck pain after 4 weeks?
* Do the two treatments differ in their effects on neck-related disability, neck position sense, breathing muscle strength, and upper trapezius muscle activity?

Researchers will compare kinesiology taping with self-sustained natural apophyseal glide (self-SNAG) mobilization to see which approach is more effective.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to one of the two treatment groups
* Receive kinesiology tape applied to the back of the neck every 4 days for 4 weeks, or learn and perform a towel-assisted neck self-mobilization exercise for 4 weeks
* Receive education on posture and self-management
* Complete assessments of pain, neck disability, neck position sense, breathing muscle strength, and neck-shoulder muscle activity at the start of the study, after 4 weeks, and 1 month later
primary_outcomes: Change in Neck Pain Intensity (Visual Analog Scale)
title: Kinesiology Taping Versus Self-Mobilization for Neck Pain Related to Prolonged Electronic Device Use

brief_summary: The Supporting Older Adults Remotely (SOAR) study is a randomized controlled trial evaluating a 12-week, telephone-delivered peer support intervention for adults age 50 and older with serious mental illness who live in supportive housing. SOAR is designed to support aging in place and improve independent living skills through structured peer support focused on medication adherence, medical and psychiatric self-management, coping, goal setting, healthcare navigation, social relationships, self-advocacy, and connection to community resources. Participants will be randomly assigned to receive either SOAR or Peer Support as Usual. Participants will complete assessments at baseline and 3, 6, and 12 months. The study will also examine factors that may help or hinder implementation and sustainability of SOAR in supportive housing.
primary_outcomes: Independent Living Skills Survey (ILSS) Score
title: Supporting Older Adults Remotely

brief_summary: The main goal of the project is to characterize the bone marrow immunological milieu and investigate potential treatment defining events of the tumor microenvironment in relapsed and refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM) patients receiving BCMA-targeted therapies.
primary_outcomes: T-cell compartment fitness at the time of disease progression
Genetic status of the BCMA locus at relapse following BCMA-targeted therapy

brief_summary: This randomized clinical trial compares two types of orthodontic brackets, self-ligating and conventional, in adults aged 18 to 25 with moderate crowding of the lower front teeth (4 to 8 mm). The main question is whether the type of bracket affects the thickness of the thin bone covering the front surface of the lower incisor roots (labial alveolar bone) during the leveling and alignment phase of treatment. Some clinicians claim that self-ligating brackets with light-force copper-nickel-titanium wires let the bone adapt and follow the teeth, while others report bone thinning with both systems. Twenty participants will be randomly assigned to self-ligating or conventional brackets. Bone thickness will be measured on cone beam computed tomography (CBCT) scans taken before treatment and at the end of leveling and alignment. The study will also compare the speed of alignment, changes in tooth inclination (torque and tip), pain, root resorption, and periodontal health between the two groups.
primary_outcomes: Change in labial alveolar bone thickness of lower anterior teeth
title: Self-ligating vs Conventional Brackets and Labial Bone Thickness During Crowding Correction in Adults

brief_summary: This research study is being conducted to study the use of artificial-intelligence powered virtual reality exposure therapy (AI-VRET) to treat college students with obsessive compulsive disorder (OCD).
interventions: Artificial Intelligence-Powered Virtual Reality Exposure Therapy (AI-VRET)
primary_outcomes: Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale-II (Y-BOCS-II)

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether MoodSync, a mobile application for patients and their family caregivers, improves mood stability, medication adherence, daily functioning and early detection of relapse warning signs in adults with severe mental illness in Bahrain. The main question it aims to answer is: Does MoodSync plus standard care improve manic symptoms, medication adherence, practical and social functioning, and early warning signs more than standard care alone?

Participants will be randomly assigned to MoodSync plus standard care or standard care alone. MoodSync participants will use the patient app for 12 weeks for daily mood check-ins, sleep and activity tracking with a wearable device, medication reminders, daily-routine (social rhythm) support and early warning-sign reporting. A nominated family caregiver may use the linked caregiver app. All participants continue standard care and complete questionnaires before and after the intervention period.

Research hypothesis:

\* Patients who use MoodSync will show greater improvement in mood symptoms, medication adherence, practical and social functioning, and relapse-related outcomes than patients receiving standard care alone.
primary_outcomes: Manic symptoms - Altman Self-Rating Mania Scale (ASRM)
Medication adherence - Morisky-Green-Levine Medication Adherence Scale (4 items)
Practical and social functioning - Practical and Social Functioning Scale (PSF)
Early warning signs of relapse - Early Signs Scale (ESS)
title: A Mobile App to Support Mood, Daily Routines and Medication Adherence in Adults With Severe Mental Illness

brief_summary:
This study aims to recruit women aged 45 years in the Netherlands to participate in a one-time breast MRI screening examination and to evaluate their motivation for participation as well as the impact of screening on their wellbeing. Recruitment will occur through public media announcements and distribution of flyers in the geeral practitioners' waiting rooms, ensuring equity and adherence to GDPR regulations. Participants will be enrolled on a first-come, first-served basis, with calls repeated every six months over an estimated three-year period. All participants will complete questionnaires assessing reasons for participation, cancer-related worry, and experiences with the screening. Outcomes will be stratified by screening result: negative, false positive, or cancer detected.

A subset of women will be contacted one year later to assess long-term effects on health beliefs. Additionally, qualitative in-depth interviews will be conducted with a subgroup of participants to explore themes related to motivation and perceived impact of participation.
primary_outcomes: Cancer Detection Rate
Tumor Size of MRI-Detected Breast Cancers
Cost per Cancer Detected
title: Screening and the Future of Enhanced MRI for Early Breast Cancer Detection

brief_summary:
Acute low back pain often resolves spontaneously, but some patients develop persistent pain and disability. The goal of this clinical trial is to determine whether Cognitive Functional Therapy (CFT), compared with usual care, can help prevent recent low back pain from becoming persistent in adults receiving direct-access physiotherapy in primary care.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does CFT reduce low back pain-related disability over 12 months compared with usual care?
* Is CFT cost-effective compared with usual care?
* What are the long-term effects of CFT compared with usual care over a 3-year follow-up period?

Researchers will compare CFT to usual care to see if CFT prevents the transition from acute to persistent low back pain.

Participants will:

* Receive either Cognitive Functional Therapy or usual care.
* Complete questionnaires at baseline and follow-up assessments throughout the study.
conditions: Acute Low Back Pain (Low Back Pain for Less Than 3 Months)
primary_outcomes: Average low back pain-related disability over 12-month follow-up
title: Preventing the Transition From Acute to Persistent Disabling Low Back Pain Through Cognitive Functional Therapy

brief_summary:
The goal of this study is to explore if preoperative ω-3 fish oil lipid emulsion parenteral nutrition (PN) can improve postoperative outcomes in patients undergoing major abdominal surgery. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does preoperative PN containing ω-3 fish oil lipid emulsion improve postoperative nutritional status (prealbumin, albumin) in patients undergoing major abdominal surgery?
* Does preoperative PN containing ω-3 fish oil lipid emulsion affect other postoperative clinical outcomes (length of hospital stay, inflammatory status, postoperative complication rates, BMI changes, liver function changes, time to first flatus and defecation) in these patients? Researchers will compare the ω-3 fish oil lipid emulsion PN group (preoperative ω-3 PN) to the control group (preoperative normal diet) to see if there are differences in postoperative nutritional status, safety, and other clinical outcomes.

Participants will:

* In the intervention group, receive preoperative parenteral nutrition containing ω-3 fish oil lipid emulsion.
* In the control group, maintain a normal preoperative diet.
* Undergo blood tests and clinical assessments at baseline (before PN use) and on postoperative days 1, 3, and 7 (or at discharge, whichever comes first).
interventions: Conventional lipid without ω-3 fish oil
lead_sponsor: Second Affiliated Hospital of Nanchang University
primary_outcomes: Serum albumin and prealbumin levels
Length of hospital stay (days)
title: Effects of Preoperative Parenteral Nutrition With Omega-3 Fish Oil Lipid Emulsion on Postoperative Outcomes in Patients Undergoing Major Abdominal Surgery

brief_summary:
This study will investigate whether heart activity and changes in the skin's ability to conduct electricity can help predict performance during a demanding computer task. These signals reflect how the body responds to mental effort. The main question is whether measurements taken at rest and near the beginning of the task help predict later accuracy, beyond information about sleep the previous night, current sleepiness, and initial task performance.

Healthy young adults will attend one visit lasting approximately 50-60 minutes. Participants will complete a questionnaire and wear sensors that record heart activity and skin responses. After a five-minute resting measurement, participants will learn a computer task involving letters and numbers. The task requires remembering the previous letter and deciding whether numbers are odd or even. A short calibration will adjust the presentation speed to each participant.

Participants will then perform the task for 16 minutes at the selected speed and rate their fatigue and the demands of the task. After these ratings, participants will rest quietly for five minutes and repeat the task for four minutes at the same speed.

The researchers will also examine how performance, fatigue, and body responses change during the task and after rest. The study is intended to improve understanding of sustained mental effort and is not a medical diagnostic assessment.
interventions: Individually Calibrated Time Load Dual-back Task With Seated Rest
primary_outcomes: Weighted Accuracy During the Final Four Minutes of the Main Cognitive Task
title: Predicting Declines in Attention and Memory During a Prolonged Mental Task

brief_summary:
Preoperative fear and anxiety are common among patients undergoing orthopedic surgery and may adversely affect perioperative outcomes. This quasi-experimental study will aim to evaluate the effectiveness of preoperative virtual reality (VR) exposure in reducing surgical fear and anxiety among adult orthopedic patients.

A non-randomized controlled pretest-posttest study will be conducted with 74 adult patients undergoing orthopedic surgery. Participants will be assigned to either a VR intervention group (n=37) or a control group (n=37). Patients in the intervention group will receive immersive nature and underwater VR content in addition to standard preoperative care, whereas those in the control group will receive standard care alone. Surgical fear and anxiety will be assessed before and after the intervention using the Surgical Fear Questionnaire (SFQ) and the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI).

The study is expected to provide evidence regarding the feasibility and potential effectiveness of VR as a safe, non-pharmacological nursing intervention for reducing preoperative anxiety and surgical fear in orthopedic patients. The findings may guide the integration of VR into preoperative nursing care and inform future randomized controlled trials with larger samples.
primary_outcomes: Change in Preoperative Surgical Fear Assessed Using the Surgical Fear Questionnaire
Change in Preoperative State Anxiety Assessed Using the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory-State Scale
title: Effects of Preoperative Virtual Reality on Surgical Fear and Anxiety in Patients

brief_summary:
The aim of this study is to compare the total and regional body composition characteristics of women with lipedema and women without lipedema who are matched for age and body mass index, as determined by the TANITA MC-580 segmental bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) device. In addition to total fat mass and fat percentage, fat mass, fat-free mass, and muscle mass measurements of the right and left legs, right and left arms, and trunk are planned to be evaluated. From these measurements, regional distribution indicators such as the proportion of lower extremity fat mass within total body fat, the leg-to-trunk fat ratio, the leg-to-arm fat ratio, and the leg muscle-to-fat ratio will be calculated. In addition, the study aims to examine the relationships between segmental body composition characteristics and disease type and stage, disease duration, pain severity, and lower extremity function in the lipedema group.

Hypothesis: The proportion of total body fat located in the lower extremities is significantly higher in women with lipedema compared to women without lipedema matched for age and body mass index.
lead_sponsor: Sultan Abdulhamid Han Training and Research Hospital, Istanbul, Turkey
primary_outcomes: Ratio of the total fat mass of the two legs to total body fat mass
title: Comparison of Segmental Body Composition Characteristics in Lipedema and Obesity

brief_summary:
This study looks at how three different numbing injections affect how quickly patients recover after knee replacement surgery (total knee arthroplasty, or TKA). Pain after knee replacement is common and can slow down how soon patients get moving again. Doctors often inject a numbing medication around the knee during surgery to help control this pain, but it is not clear which medication helps patients recover fastest in the first few days after surgery.

The study compares three injections that are all FDA approved and already used as part of routine knee replacement care: Exparel (liposomal bupivacaine), Zynrelef (bupivacaine with meloxicam), and Marcaine (bupivacaine). Exparel and Zynrelef are the two groups being studied, and Marcaine is the comparison (control) group.

Adults who are already planning to have a knee replacement may take part. People who join are placed into one of the three injection groups at random, so each person has a one in three chance of receiving each injection. Patients are not told which injection they received. Everything else about the surgery, anesthesia, and recovery care stays the same as usual.

The main goal is to see which injection helps patients recover best in the first three days after surgery. To measure recovery, the study team collects information on pain, pain-medication use, knee motion, activity level, and function. Patients complete short questionnaires about their activity, pain, and quality of life at their regular visits (before surgery and at 3 days, 1 week, 2 weeks, 6 weeks, 3 months, 1 year, and 2 years). A smart knee implant also records information about knee movement and motion at 3 and 7 days after surgery. About 200 people will take part. The study is considered minimal risk, meaning the risks are similar to those of having a knee replacement outside of the study.
interventions: Intra-articular injection of bupivacaine in the knee joint
intra-articular injection of Exparel in the knee joint
lead_sponsor: Foundation for Orthopaedic Research and Education
primary_outcomes: Early Functional Recovery
title: Smart Knee Evaluation of Exparel and Zynrelef in TKA Recovery

brief_summary:
This observational study aims to evaluate the reliability and validity of the Uzbek-language versions of three questionnaires used to assess men's health: the Androgen Deficiency in Aging Males (ADAM), Aging Males' Symptoms (AMS), and International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS).

The study will include approximately 400 men aged 35-59 years from the Andijan region of Uzbekistan. Participants will complete all three questionnaires electronically using Google Forms. At least 120 participants will complete the questionnaires again after 7-14 days to assess the consistency of their responses.

Blood samples will be collected to measure total testosterone levels and examine their relationship with questionnaire results. The study will also assess how well ADAM identifies men with low testosterone levels and how reliably AMS and IPSS measure their respective symptoms.

No treatment or experimental intervention will be administered. The findings will help determine whether these Uzbek-language questionnaires are suitable for use in clinical practice and future research.
conditions: Psychometric Validation of Men's Health Questionnaires
primary_outcomes: Structural Validity of the Uzbek-Language AMS Questionnaire
Structural Validity of the Uzbek-Language IPSS Questionnaire
Test-Retest Agreement of the Uzbek-Language ADAM Questionnaire
title: Validation of Uzbek-Language ADAM, AMS, and IPSS Questionnaires in Men Aged 35-59 Years

brief_summary: This randomized controlled clinical trial will include patients indicated for endodontic microsurgery due to persistent periapical lesions. Participants will be randomly allocated into two groups. Preoperative CBCT will be taken for each patient, and patients will be scheduled for endodontic microsurgery. Preoperative gingival crevicular fluid samples will be collected. During the surgical procedure the test group will receive application of BBL as a final flush to the bony cavity and surface conditioning of the root end before closure of the surgical site, while the control group will undergo conventional microsurgery without BBL. Standardized surgical procedures will be followed in both groups. Postoperative pain will be assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) at defined time points following surgery. Inflammatory mediator expressions (e.g., IL-1β and TNF α) will be evaluated using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) in comparison to preoperative samples to assess the inflammatory response associated with healing at 10th day postsurgical followed by soft tissue healing clinical assessment using Early Healing Score (EHS). Bone healing will be assessed radiographically using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) at 6-month follow-ups, with quantitative three-dimensional analysis of lesion volume reduction
conditions: Patients Diagnosed With Persistent Apical Periodontitis in Maxillary Anterior Regions Require Endodontic Microsurgery
primary_outcomes: Periapical bone healing assessed radiographically using CBCT
title: Bone-Bioactive Liquid as an Adjunct in Endodontic Surgery

brief_summary: This is a multicenter, medical-record-based, retrospective observational study of approximately 400 patients with high-grade osteosarcoma treated at four sites in the Republic of Korea. The study describes treatment patterns and survival outcomes (event-free survival \[EFS\], progression-free survival \[PFS\], and overall survival \[OS\]) in patients who completed or discontinued first-line treatment for high-grade osteosarcoma, irrespective of complete remission status. The primary objective is to retrospectively estimate the 12-month EFS rate, calculated from the date of diagnosis, in the full cohort of high-grade osteosarcoma patients. Key secondary objectives evaluate EFS and OS from the date of confirmed complete remission/no evidence of disease (CR/NED) in the subset of clinically high-risk patients who achieve CR/NED, in order to establish a historical reference data supporting the design and interpretation of a future prospective clinical trial of vactosertib as maintenance therapy.
primary_outcomes: 12-month Event-Free Survival (EFS) rate
title: Treatment Patterns and Survival Outcomes in High-Grade Osteosarcoma: A Multicenter Retrospective Study

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether two types of ultrasound-guided nerve block, the intertransverse process block and the erector spinae plane block, reduce pain and the need for opioid pain medicines during and after lumbar spine surgery in adults. It also compares the two blocks with each other.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Do patients who receive either nerve block need less morphine in the first 24 hours after surgery than patients who receive only local anesthetic injected at the skin incision? Is there a difference between the two nerve blocks in pain scores, the amount of opioid medicine needed during and after surgery, the time until patients first ask for pain medicine, and side effects?

Researchers will compare three groups: an erector spinae plane block group, an intertransverse process block group, and a control group that receives local anesthetic infiltration at the incision site.

Participants will:

Be randomly assigned to one of the three groups before surgery Receive the nerve block on both sides of the spine with ropivacaine before general anesthesia (block groups), or local anesthetic infiltration along the planned incision after induction of anesthesia (control group) Undergo general anesthesia and lumbar spine surgery following the same standard protocol Use a patient-controlled analgesia pump that delivers morphine on demand for 24 hours after surgery Rate their pain at rest and during movement at set times over the first 24 hours, and be monitored for side effects such as nausea and vomiting
primary_outcomes: Cumulative Morphine Consumption Within 24 Hours After Surgery
title: Intertransverse Process Block Versus Erector Spinae Plane Block for Pain Relief in Lumbar Spine Surgery

brief_summary:
This study aimed to evaluate clinical and periapical radiographic healing following endodontic surgery using a surgical microscope.

An uncontrolled longitudinal clinical intervention study was conducted in patients requiring endodontic surgery. All surgical procedures were performed using a surgical microscope, ultrasonic instruments, and mineral trioxide aggregate (MTA) root-end filling.

Postoperative healing was evaluated through clinical examinations and periapical radiographs at scheduled follow-up visits over a 3-month period. The study assessed clinical healing, radiographic healing, changes in periapical radiolucency, and overall treatment success.
lead_sponsor: University of Medicine and Pharmacy at Ho Chi Minh City
primary_outcomes: Clinical Healing
Radiographic Healing
title: Clinical and Radiographic Healing After Microscope-Assisted Endodontic Surgery

brief_summary:
Background: Studies highlight the potential benefits of home-based exercise for cancer survivors with chemotherapy-induced neuropathy (CIN); however, its effectiveness in alleviating CIN-related sensorimotor impairments and symptoms has been inconsistent and generally modest. Non-invasive vagus nerve stimulation (nVNS) has emerged as a promising adjunct for CIN rehabilitation. Preliminary studies suggest that nVNS can enhance the therapeutic effects of exercise-based rehabilitation, leading to greater improvements in sensorimotor impairments. A recent trial found that nVNS alleviated CIN-related pain and improved mental well-being, but did not significantly enhance physical well-being or clinician-rated CIN severity.

Objectives: To evaluate the efficacy, safety, and feasibility of combining home-based exercise with non-invasive vagus nerve stimulation (nVNS) to alleviate chemotherapy-induced neuropathy (CIN) and improve quality of life in cancer survivors.

Design and Subjects: This phase II randomized controlled trial will enroll 60 cancer survivors with established CIN following treatment with platinum compounds or taxanes. Participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to one of three groups: exercise with real nVNS (ERS), exercise with sham nVNS (ESS), or usual care.

Interventions: Participants in the experimental groups will engage in a 12-week home-based exercise program, with the ERS group receiving real nVNS and the ESS group receiving sham stimulation.

Study Instruments and Main Outcome Measures: The primary outcome, patient-reported CIN, will be assessed using the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire-Chemotherapy-Induced Peripheral Neuropathy 20-item (EORTC QLQ-CIPN20). Secondary outcomes will include the Total Neuropathy Score-nurse for clinician-reported CIN, the Symptom Distress Scale for general symptoms, functional performance measures (Timed Up and Go Test and 6-Minute Walk Test), and the EORTC QLQ-Core 30-item for quality of life.

Data Analysis and Expected Results: Generalized Estimating Equations will be used for efficacy outcome analysis. It is anticipated that the combined intervention may lead to improvements in CIN, functioning, and quality of life, thereby supporting further research in larger trials.
interventions: Home-based aerobic and resistance exercise program
primary_outcomes: Patient-Reported Chemotherapy-Induced Neuropathy as Assessed by the Chinese Version of the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire-Chemotherapy-Induced Peripheral Neuropathy (EORTC QLQ-CIPN20)
title: Home-Based Exercise and Vagus Nerve Stimulation for Chemotherapy-Induced Neuropathy

brief_summary:
The goal of this single-arm, prospective clinical trial is to assess the clinical efficacy and safety of oral Aeromonas sp. MTB-specific phage therapy in adult participants aged 18-70 years with pouchitis following ileal pouch-anal anastomosis (IPAA) for ulcerative colitis, who are positive for stool MTB bacteria or aerolysin.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does 2-week oral MTB phage treatment lead to mPDAI-defined pouchitis remission at Week 14?
* What is the safety profile of oral MTB phage intervention in this patient population? No external control group is utilised; baseline data of each participant serves as self-control.

Participants will:

* Receive once-daily oral MTB phage (one bottle, 30 minutes post-meal) for 14 consecutive days.
* Complete mPDAI symptom questionnaires and IBDQ quality-of-life assessments at baseline and follow-up time-points (Weeks 2, 8, 14, 24, 34).
* Provide stool specimens for measurement of faecal phage titre, MTB bacterial load and aerolysin level at 24-48 hours post-initial phage administration, Weeks 2, 8, 14, 24 and 34.
* Undergo pouch endoscopy for mPDAI endoscopic scoring at baseline, Week 14 and Week 34.
* Complete scheduled follow-up up to Week 34, with continuous monitoring of vital signs, laboratory parameters and all adverse events throughout the study period.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of participants with a decrease in Modified Pouchitis Disease Activity Index (mPDAI) total score from baseline to week 14
title: This is a Single-center, Prospective, Single-arm Clinical Study Designed to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Oral Aeromonas sp. MTB Phage Therapy for Pouchitis in Patients With Ulcerative Colitis (UC).

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn how a community-based peer counselling service works in everyday practice and whether it helps people who are going through a psychologically difficult time. Peer counsellors are trained people with their own lived experience of mental health problems. The service, Peerberatung St. Gallen, already exists in St. Gallen, Switzerland. It offers up to six one-hour counselling sessions per year per client. The study does not change the service or decide who receives it.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

* Do clients report changes in their personal recovery, well-being and stress after using the service?
* How do clients experience the counseling, and what do they find helpful?
* How is the service put into practice, and how do peer counsellors and partner organizations view it?

Clients who use the service will:

* Fill out an anonymous questionnaire at the start of counseling and again after their last session
* Be invited to take part in an interview about their experience

Peer counsellors and staff of partner organizations will:

\- Fill out a questionnaire about how acceptable, appropriate and practical they find the service Be invited to take part in group discussions (peers) or interviews (staff of organizations)
primary_outcomes: Acceptability of the peer counseling service (Acceptability of Intervention Measure, AIM)
Appropriateness of the peer counseling service (Intervention Appropriateness Measure, IAM)
Feasibility of the peer counseling service (Feasibility of Intervention Measure, FIM)
Facilitators and barriers to implementation of the peer counseling service
title: A Community-based, Peer-led Counseling Service: A Hybrid Type 3 Effectiveness-implementation Study

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if a community-based health education and communication program helps prevent and reduce depression in older adults living in Ho Chi Minh City. It will also evaluate how the program affects quality of life and caregiver stress.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. Does the health education program improve knowledge, attitudes, and practice regarding depression among older adults and their primary caregivers?
2. Does the program reduce depression scores (measured by GDS-30) and improve quality of life in older adults compared to standard care?
3. Does the program help lower caregiving burden and stress among primary caregivers?

Researchers will compare an intervention group (older adult and caregiver pairs who receive the education program) to a control group (pairs who receive standard community health care).

Participants in the intervention group will:

* Attend 5 group education sessions (45-60 minutes each) covering early depression detection, sleep hygiene, nutrition, physical activity, stress management, and caregiver support.
* Complete questionnaires at the start and end of the program to measure depression symptoms, quality of life, caregiving burden, and health knowledge.
lead_sponsor: University of Medicine and Pharmacy at Ho Chi Minh City
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Geriatric Depression Scale (30-item) Total Score at 3-6 Months
Change From Baseline in Zarit Burden Interview (22-item) Total Score at 6 Months
Change From Baseline in World Health Organization Quality of Life-BREF Scores at Post-Intervention

brief_summary:
This study looks at a heart procedure called transcatheter mitral valve replacement. Doctors use a device called SAPIEN M3 to replace a damaged heart valve. The valve is replaced without open-heart surgery, through thin tubes guided to the heart.

One step of the procedure can be harder in some patients. The new valve must be guided into place by a part called a "dock." In certain patients, the dock can land too low. This is called a "dock drop." It can make the procedure less successful.

Doctors developed a new technique to prevent this problem. It is called the double transseptal guide sheath (DGS) technique. It uses two thin tubes during the procedure, instead of one. The two tubes lift the dock into a better position before the new valve is placed.

Researchers reviewed medical records from 77 patients. These patients were treated at 16 hospitals across Europe. Some patients had heart anatomy that put them at higher risk for a low dock. These patients received the double-tube technique. Other patients received the standard, single-tube technique.

The double-tube technique raised the dock to a safer position. This position was similar to patients with naturally lower-risk heart anatomy. The technique did not cause more complications than the standard technique.

These findings suggest the double-tube technique may help prevent a low dock. This may benefit patients with higher-risk heart anatomy during this procedure.
primary_outcomes: Composite Primary Safety Endpoint
Post-Procedural Echocardiographic Efficacy Outcomes
title: Double Transseptal Guide Sheath to Prevent Dock Drop During SAPIEN M3 Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement

brief_summary: Background: Complete decongestive therapy (CDT) is the standard treatment for lymphedema, but response varies by localization and laterality. Data on segmental distribution of therapeutic response and predictors of response are limited. Objective: To evaluate changes in lymphedema indicators after intensive-phase CDT, compare therapeutic response profiles across clinical subgroups, and develop a predictive model of response. Methods: Retrospective observational cohort study of 111 patients with secondary lymphedema: unilateral upper extremity, unilateral lower extremity, bilateral lower extremity. Primary outcome: percentage reduction of excess indicator (PREI) for unilateral groups and relative reduction of sum of circumferences (ΣC) for bilateral group. Secondary outcomes: topographic response profile (7 anatomical points), proportion of clinical responders (≥10%), predictive factors, and predictive model. Expected results: Identification of topographic heterogeneity of response, determination of factors of CDT resistance (especially in bilateral lymphedema), development of a validated predictive model for therapy personalization.
conditions: Lower Extremity Lymphedema After Gynecologic Cancer Surgery
interventions: Intensive phase of Complete Decongestive Therapy
primary_outcomes: Percentage Reduction of Limb Excess Size
title: Efficacy of Complete Decongestive Therapy for Limb Lymphedema: Response Profile and Predictive Modeling

It aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Firmonertinib combined with chemotherapy in patients with unresectable Stage III lung adenocarcinoma harboring EGFR PACC mutations. brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate whether chronopharmacokinetic model-guided individualized unequal twice-daily tacrolimus dosing improves renal allograft function and reduces acute rejection in stable kidney transplant recipients. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does chrono-individualized tacrolimus dosing preserve graft renal function (eGFR) compared with conventional equal twice-daily dosing? Does chrono-individualized tacrolimus dosing lower the incidence of acute rejection in kidney transplant recipients? Researchers will compare recipients receiving chronopharmacokinetic-guided "low morning, high evening" individualized tacrolimus doses to recipients receiving conventional equal twice-daily tacrolimus doses to see if the chrono-individualized regimen improves renal function and reduces acute rejection risk.

Participants will:

Be randomly assigned to one of two tacrolimus dosing groups at a 1:1 ratio Receive routine immunosuppressive therapy and follow-up for 12 months Undergo blood sampling for tacrolimus concentration, calcineurin activity and multi-omics biomarker detection Complete regular clinical assessments of graft function, adverse events and rejection episodes
interventions: Chronotherapy-based individualized low-morning high-evening tacrolimus dosing

Change in graft renal function (eGFR, calculated using the Cockcroft-Gault equation)

brief_summary:
This study compared ketorolac and dexmedetomidine when added to lignocaine to prevent pain caused by a tourniquet during intravenous regional anesthesia. This technique involved injecting a local anesthetic into a vein to numb an arm or leg for surgery. A tourniquet, a tight cuff placed around the limb, restricted blood flow but could cause pain during the procedure.

The study was conducted at Mayo Hospital, Lahore, and was designed to include 70 patients aged 18-60 years undergoing surgery on the lower part of an arm or leg. Two treatment groups of 35 patients each received lignocaine with either dexmedetomidine or ketorolac. Pain was assessed on a scale from 0 to 10 at 15, 30, and 45 minutes after tourniquet application. Additional pain relief was administered when the pain score reached 4 or higher.
primary_outcomes: Mean Time to First Rescue Analgesic Requirement
title: Comparison of Ketorolac and Dexmedetomidine as An Adjunct to Lignocaine in Prevention of Tourniquet Induced Pain During Intravenous Regional Anesthesia

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn how pregnancy after bariatric surgery affects the nutritional status of mothers and their babies. The study will also look at pregnancy complications and the best time to get pregnant after surgery. It includes pregnant women who have had bariatric surgery and compares them to pregnant women who have not had surgery.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Do women who have had bariatric surgery have more vitamin and mineral deficiencies during pregnancy? Are pregnancy complications like preterm birth or high blood pressure more common after bariatric surgery? Do babies born to mothers who had bariatric surgery have different growth or nutrient levels?

Researchers will compare women with and without bariatric surgery to see if there are differences in:

Nutrient levels in blood and urine Pregnancy outcomes like gestational diabetes or preeclampsia Baby's birth weight, length, and vitamin levels

Participants will:

Give blood and urine samples during pregnancy and after birth Answer questions about their diet and health Have their weight and body composition measured Use a glucose monitor during pregnancy This study will help improve care for women who become pregnant after bariatric surgery.
interventions: Post-Bariatric Maternal and Infant Health Study
primary_outcomes: Maternal Iron status
Maternal gestational weight gain following bariatric surgery, compared with non-operated controls.
title: Mother and Offspring's Nutritional Status -Pregnancy After Maternal Bariatric Surgery

brief_summary: Blood pressure is an important part of checking heart health. Blood pressure is usually measured while sitting, but in everyday medical care it is sometimes measured in other positions, such as the Fowler position, where the upper body is raised. This study will compare blood pressure measured while sitting with blood pressure measured in the Fowler position to see whether the results are similar enough to be considered equivalent. Adults aged 18 or older who can give informed consent and have an arm circumference of 22-42 cm may take part. Each participant will have their blood pressure measured in both positions, with the order chosen randomly. People who cannot maintain the required positions or whose condition could affect the accuracy of the blood pressure measurement will not take part.
lead_sponsor: Iuliu Hatieganu University of Medicine and Pharmacy
primary_outcomes: Mean paired difference in systolic blood pressure
title: Equivalence of Systolic Blood Pressure Measurements Between Fowler and Seated Positions

brief_summary:
Bodybuilders present unique body composition profiles, characterized by high fat-free mass and very low levels of body fat. In addition, many competitive and non-competitive athletes use anabolic-androgenic steroids (AAS) and fat-burning pharmacological agents to enhance muscle mass and accelerate fat loss.

Accurate determination of energy requirements is critical for performance and nutritional planning in this population. Resting metabolic rate (RMR) represents the largest component of daily energy expenditure. While indirect calorimetry is considered the reference method to assess RMR, it is expensive and not widely accessible, making predictive mathematical equations the primary tool used in sports and clinical settings. However, widely used equations (such as Harris-Benedict, Mifflin-St Jeor, and Cunningham) were developed in general or non-athletic populations and may systematically underestimate energy requirements in bodybuilders using performance-enhancing substances.

The primary aim of this cross-sectional study is to measure resting metabolic rate via indirect calorimetry and body composition via dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) in adult bodybuilders using anabolic and fat-burning agents. The ultimate goal is to develop and validate a population-specific predictive equation for RMR and compare its accuracy against established predictive formulas.
primary_outcomes: Resting Metabolic Rate
title: Resting Metabolic Rate in Bodybuilders Using Performance-Enhancing Drugs

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to assess whether finding pelvic neutral before or during an isometric loaded task will influence the muscle recruitment pattern between local and global core musculature. The loaded tasks are a prone plank, side plank, and glute bridge. The local musculature being investigated are the internal oblique and multifidus, and the global musculature being investigated are the rectus abdominis and lateral erector spinae. Participants will complete maximal voluntary contractions (MVCs) for the rectus abdominis and internal oblique along with lateral erector spinae and multifidus. Participants will view a standardized video demonstration of anterior pelvic tilt, posterior pelvic tilt, and neutral pelvic tilt positioning and will practice finding each position. Participants will complete a prone plank, right and left side plank, and glute bridge with pelvic neutral set prior to loading the exercise position and with pelvic neutral set after assuming the loaded exercise position. The exercise and condition order will be randomized, and muscle activity will be recorded using surface electromyography.
primary_outcomes: Core Muscle Activation
title: Core Muscle Activation With Pelvic Neutral Positioning in Division I Soccer Athletes

brief_summary:
Lynch syndrome is the most common inherited condition that raises a person's risk of getting certain cancers. It happens because of changes in genes that normally fix damaged DNA. People with Lynch syndrome have a higher chance over their lifetime of cancers like bowel, womb (endometrial), ovarian, and others.

For people with a uterus, cancer of the womb lining (endometrial cancer) is often the first cancer to appear, affecting over 40% of some groups.

Even though the risk is high, the current ways of checking for endometrial cancer aren't ideal. They often involve uncomfortable and invasive tests, like taking tissue samples (biopsies) or internal scans. These can be expensive and don't always catch cancer early, so many people don't keep up with regular checks.

New methods are being developed that look for tiny amounts of cancer DNA in easy, non-invasive samples, like urine or self-collected vaginal swabs. These approaches could make testing easier, more comfortable, and possibly just as accurate.

The PREDI-ENDO study will compare these simple tests (urine and self-collected swabs) with the standard, more invasive tests. It will include people with Lynch syndrome, those who may have symptoms, and those who would rather avoid invasive procedures. Researchers will also compare different types of samples to see which works best.

About 400 women across around 20 sites in the UK will be asked to take part. They'll do these new tests alongside their usual hospital tests to see if screening can be made easier and better.

The goal is to develop safer, simpler, and more reliable ways to find cancer early, and possibly replace the current invasive tests in the future.
primary_outcomes: To define the diagnostic accuracy of non-invasive surveillance approaches for EC detection and assess non-inferiority to standard surveillance using invasive modalities.
title: Protocol for Non-invasive Gynaecological Surveillance in Lynch Syndrome

brief_summary: The goal of this randomized controlled trial is to learn whether an ultrasound-guided quadro-iliac plane block (QIPB) reduces opioid use and pain after laparoscopic inguinal hernia repair in adults aged 18-65 years. All participants will receive the same general anesthesia, multimodal analgesia and intravenous tramadol patient-controlled analgesia (PCA). brief_summary:
This randomized, controlled clinical study will evaluate the effect of an ultrasound-guided PECS II block on postoperative pain control in patients undergoing elective augmentation mammoplasty.

A total of 50 adult female patients aged 18-65 years who meet the eligibility criteria and provide written informed consent are planned to be enrolled. Participants will be randomly assigned to two groups using a computer-generated randomization method.

Participants in the PECS II group will receive an ultrasound-guided PECS II block after induction of general anesthesia and before surgical incision, in addition to standard postoperative multimodal analgesia. Participants in the control group will receive standard postoperative multimodal analgesia without a PECS II block or placebo procedure.

The primary objective is to evaluate postoperative pain intensity using the visual analog scale (VAS) at 1, 6, 12, and 24 hours after surgery. Secondary outcomes will include analgesic consumption, additional analgesic requirements, postoperative nausea and vomiting, and potential complications associated with the block.

Outcomes will be compared between the two groups to assess the effect of the PECS II block on postoperative pain control.
conditions: Postoperative Pain After Breast Augmentation Surgery
primary_outcomes: Postoperative Pain Intensity Measured by Visual Analog Scale (VAS)
title: Effect of Adding Ultrasound-Guided PECS II Block to Standard Multimodal Analgesia in Breast Augmentation Surgery

brief_summary:
Background:

Many different research projects need a steady supply of human blood. Blood donated by screened, healthy people may be used to test new drugs, for example, or to learn how blood cells work. Scientists from the National Institutes of Health and the Food and Drug Administration want to collect blood from donors for use in laboratory studies.

Objective:

To collect blood and blood parts from healthy donors for research.

Eligibility:

Healthy people aged 18 years and older who weigh more than 110 pounds. They must meet the requirements to donate blood for research.

Participants will be screened. A nurse will check their general health. The veins in both arms will be checked to make sure they are good for donation.

Participants may donate whole blood as often as they wish, but no more than 2 cups will be taken over an 8-week period. At each visit, they will fill out a questionnaire about their health, and a small sample of blood will be tested to make sure it is safe to donate.

Participants may also opt to donate only white blood cells. They will undergo leukapheresis: Blood will be taken from the body through a needle inserted into a vein. The blood will pass through a machine that separates out the white blood cells. The remaining blood will be returned to the body through a different needle.

Those who donate white blood cells called granulocytes may need to take 2 drugs, including a steroid, the day before. Participants who repeat this donation will need an eye exam.

Participants may remain in the study for 20 years.
lead_sponsor: National Institutes of Health Clinical Center (CC)
primary_outcomes: Provision of samples to researchers
title: Collection and Distribution of Blood Components From Healthy Donors for In Vitro Research Use

brief_summary: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a metabolic stress-related liver injury closely associated with insulin resistance, with a global prevalence of approximately 25%. It may progress to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), which can lead to cirrhosis, end-stage liver disease, and increased cardiovascular risk, representing a major unmet medical need. Thyroid hormone receptor beta (THRβ) is predominantly expressed in the liver; selective agonism regulates hepatic lipid metabolism, reduces fat accumulation, suppresses hepatic inflammation and fibrosis, and may delay MASH progression. Kylo-0603 is a liver-targeted, highly selective THRβ agonist modified with GalNAc to enrich hepatic exposure and reduce peripheral effects. This multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2a study will evaluate the efficacy, safety, and pharmacokinetics of once-daily oral Kylo-0603 capsules in approximately 120 participants with MASLD and overweight or obesity. Participants will be randomized 1:1:1:1 to Kylo-0603 8 mg, 12 mg, 16 mg, or placebo for 12 weeks. The primary endpoint is the percentage change from baseline in liver fat content assessed by MRI-PDFF at Week 12.
lead_sponsor: Shanghai Chia Tai Tianqing Pharmaceutical Technology Development Co., Ltd.
primary_outcomes: The percentage change from baseline in liver fat content
title: A Phase 2a Study of Kylo-0603 Capsule in Participants With Metabolic Dysfunction Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD)

brief_summary: In elderly patients undergoing arthroplasty surgery, postoperative recovery quality is closely related to preoperative physical reserve. Sarcopenia and reduced muscle quality can increase postoperative complications. This prospective observational study aims to investigate whether preoperative Handgrip Strength (HGS) and muscle stiffness measured by Shear Wave Elastography (SWE) can predict the quality of recovery at postoperative 24 hours (assessed via the Quality of Recovery-15 \[QoR-15T\] score) in patients aged 60 and older undergoing elective total knee or hip arthroplasty.
primary_outcomes: Postoperative Quality of Recovery Score (QoR-15T)
title: Preoperative Muscle Stiffness, Functional Reserve, and Postoperative Quality of Recovery in Lower Extremity Arthroplasty

brief_summary:
This is a Phase I clinical trial (protocol number: YR-011-B07) sponsored by Hangzhou Yirui Pharmaceutical Technology Co., Ltd., focusing on the novel oral small-molecule drug YR011 (active ingredient: PA032, a Kv1.3 channel blocker). The trial aims to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics (PK) of YR011 in healthy adult participants.

The trial has two stages: Single Ascending Dose (SAD) and Multiple Ascending Dose (MAD), with about 64 participants total (32 per stage). Participants are divided into 4 cohorts per stage (8 people per cohort), randomized 6:2 to receive YR011 or placebo in a double-blind manner. For the SAD stage, 4 dose levels are tested as a single oral dose under fasting conditions; for the MAD stage, 4 dose levels are given twice daily for 7 days plus one extra dose on Day 8.

Key procedures include screening (up to 28 days before enrollment), baseline assessments, drug administration, and follow-up (7 days for SAD, 14 days for MAD). Safety is the primary endpoint (measured by treatment-related adverse events), with secondary endpoints including PK parameters (e.g., plasma concentration, half-life) and dose accumulation. Eligible participants are 18-60 years old, healthy, and able to comply with trial procedures; those with major diseases, drug allergies, or recent medication use are excluded.

The trial follows ICH-GCP and FDA regulations, with a Safety Review Committee overseeing dose escalation and safety monitoring. All data is collected via electronic case report forms (eCRFs) and kept confidential.
interventions: Kv1.3 potassium channel blocker (PA032, investigational oral small-molecule drug)
lead_sponsor: Hangzhou Yirui Pharmaceutical Technology Co., Ltd
primary_outcomes: The incidence of treatment- Emergent adverse events (TEAE)
title: A First-in-Human SAD and MAD Study in HV to Evaluate Oral YR011 Tablet

brief_summary:
Falls are a major health concern among older adults and can lead to injuries, reduced independence, and a lower quality of life. In addition to physical changes associated with aging, an individual's confidence in preventing falls, maintaining balance, and managing situations during and after a fall may influence daily activities and social participation.

The Multidimensional Falls Efficacy Scale (MdFES) is a questionnaire designed to assess older adults' confidence in performing everyday activities without falling. It includes activities related to both daily living and participation in the community. A culturally adapted and reliable Turkish version of this questionnaire is needed to assess fall-related self-efficacy in Turkish-speaking older adults.

The aim of this study is to adapt the MdFES into Turkish and evaluate its validity, reliability, and other measurement properties in older adults. The study will examine whether the Turkish version measures fall-related self-efficacy appropriately and provides consistent results.

The findings may provide researchers and healthcare professionals with a useful assessment tool for evaluating fall-related self-efficacy in older adults. This may support the identification of individuals who lack confidence in performing daily activities and contribute to research and clinical approaches aimed at improving confidence, independence, and participation in everyday life.
primary_outcomes: Internal Consistency and Test-Retest Reliability of the Turkish MdFES
title: Turkish Adaptation of the Multidimensional Falls Efficacy Scale in Older Adults

brief_summary:
Severe mental illness (SMI), including schizophrenia spectrum disorders and bipolar disorder, is associated with significant impairments in psychosocial functioning, daily life participation, self-efficacy, and social functioning. Despite pharmacological treatment, many individuals continue to experience limitations in social relationships, occupational roles, independent living activities, and overall functioning. Psychosocial rehabilitation interventions are therefore important components of comprehensive mental health care.

Occupational therapy aims to improve individuals' participation in meaningful daily activities, enhance occupational performance, strengthen social roles, and support recovery. However, evidence regarding the effects of occupational therapy interventions on internalized stigma, self-efficacy, and personal and social functioning among individuals with SMI remains limited.

This randomized controlled trial aims to investigate the effects of a structured occupational therapy group intervention on internalized stigma, self-efficacy, personal and social functioning, occupational performance, and instrumental activities of daily living in individuals with SMI receiving services at a Community Mental Health Center. Eligible participants will be randomly assigned to either an intervention group or a control group. The intervention group will participate in a seven-session occupational therapy group program, with one 60-90-minute session per week, while the control group will continue to receive routine Community Mental Health Center services.

The intervention addresses self-awareness and identity, internalized stigma, personal strengths and self-efficacy, daily life roles, role performance, goal setting, and social participation through structured group activities and psychoeducational components. Outcomes will be assessed before the intervention and after the seven-week intervention period using validated measures of internalized stigma, self-efficacy, personal and social functioning, occupational performance and satisfaction, and instrumental activities of daily living.

It is hypothesized that participants receiving the occupational therapy intervention will demonstrate reduced internalized stigma and improved self-efficacy and personal and social functioning compared with participants receiving routine services alone.
primary_outcomes: Change in Internalized Stigma of Mental Illness Scale (ISMI) Score
Change in General Self-Efficacy Scale Score
Change in Personal and Social Performance Scale (PSP) Score
Change in Canadian Occupational Performance Measure (COPM) Scores
Change in Lawton-Brody Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADL) Score
title: Effect of Occupational Therapy on Psychosocial Parameters and Functioning in Individuals With Severe Mental Illness

brief_summary:
This study was aimed to evaluate the effects of a nurse-led, school-based structured mental health education program on adolescents' beliefs toward mental illness, social distance, and empathic tendency. The research hypotheses of this study are as follows:

H1. Adolescents receiving nurse-led, school-based structured mental health education would demonstrate a greater reduction in negative beliefs toward mental illness than adolescents in the control group.

H2. Adolescents receiving nurse-led, school-based structured mental health education would demonstrate a greater reduction in social distance toward individuals with mental illness than adolescents in the control group.

H3. Adolescents receiving nurse-led, school-based structured mental health education would demonstrate a greater increase in empathic tendency than adolescents in the control group. This study hypothesized that participation in Nurse-Led School-Based Structured Mental Health Education would reduce adolescents' misconceptions and negative beliefs about mental illness, increase their willingness to establish social relationships with individuals with mental illness, and strengthen their tendency to understand others' feelings and thoughts, consider different perspectives, and demonstrate sensitivity toward others' experiences. The study compared the intervention group, which received Nurse-Led School-Based Structured Mental Health Education, with the control group, which continued the routine school program, in terms of these variables.

Participants in the intervention group attended nurse-led, school-based structured mental health education at an Anatolian high school over a six-week period. The program was delivered once a week, on either Monday, Wednesday, or Friday, according to the students' class schedules. Each session lasted approximately 45 minutes.
interventions: Nurse-Led School-Based Structured Mental Health Education
primary_outcomes: Beliefs Toward Mental Illness total mean score
Social distance toward individuals with mental illness total mean score
Empathic tendency total mean score
title: Effects of Nurse-Led School-Based Mental Health Education on Beliefs Toward Mental Illness, Social Distance, and Empathy in Adolescents

brief_summary:
Difficult-to-treat inflammatory bowel disease (DTT-IBD) represents a heterogeneous group of patients with treatment-refractory, structurally complicated, postoperative, perianal, pouch-related, or psychosocially complex disease. This multicentre ambidirectional observational cohort will establish a longitudinal registry of adults with inflammatory bowel disease and systematically identify patients meeting prespecified DTT-IBD criteria. Clinical data will be reconstructed retrospectively and collected prospectively using a common data dictionary, including disease phenotype, advanced-therapy exposure and failure, objective disease assessments, multidisciplinary decision-making, treatment implementation, surgery, hospitalization, and long-term outcomes.

The registry will characterize the occurrence, clinical domains, treatment trajectories, longitudinal disease-control states, and outcomes of DTT-IBD. No treatment, diagnostic test, dose, surgery, or monitoring procedure will be assigned by the study. Clinical management will remain entirely at the discretion of the treating physicians and patients. The platform is designed to support prespecified nested studies addressing treatment-failure mechanisms and clinical decisions, longitudinal DTT trajectories and cumulative uncontrolled disease, and implementation of multidisciplinary care.
interventions: Routine IBD Management and Advanced-Therapy Exposure
lead_sponsor: First Affiliated Hospital, Sun Yat-Sen University
primary_outcomes: Prevalence of Difficult-to-Treat Inflammatory Bowel Disease
Cumulative Incidence of Newly Developed Difficult-to-Treat Inflammatory Bowel Disease
title: Longitudinal Registry of Difficult-to-Treat Inflammatory Bowel Disease

This study will evaluate the effects of posture-focused exercises on spinal alignment in patients with ankylosing spondylitis. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. The control group will receive a standard breathing exercise program. The intervention group will receive posture-focused exercises in addition to the standard breathing exercise program.

Spinal alignment will be evaluated using rasterstereographic analysis with the DIERS formetric 4D system. Clinical and functional outcomes will include disease activity, spinal mobility, functional status, quality of life, walking capacity, perceived exertion, and gait parameters.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate whether a combined artistic and motor activity program can reduce anxiety in children aged 8-13 with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) undergoing chemotherapy at Children's Cancer Hospital Egypt 57357. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does participation in the program reduce anxiety compared to standard care?
* Does the program improve psychological well-being, social interaction, and coping during treatment? Researchers will compare an experimental group (receiving the artistic and motor program) with a control group (receiving standard care only) to see if the intervention lowers anxiety scores on the Spence Children's Anxiety Scale.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to either the experimental or control group.
* Complete pre- and post-intervention anxiety assessments.

In the experimental group:

* Attend 16 weekly sessions over 4 months.
* Participate in art workshops (drawing, coloring, group activities).
* Engage in motor activities (warm-up, progressive exercises, relaxation, light games, treadmill/cycling up to 5 minutes).

In the control group:

Will not be exposed to the program, with anxiety measured before and after the same period.
primary_outcomes: Spence Children's Anxiety Scale, Arabic translation by Dr. Abdel Aziz Mousa
title: Artistic and Movement Activities to Reduce Anxiety in Children With Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia.

brief_summary: This is a retrospective study using archived tumor tissue and medical records from patients with cervical neuroendocrine carcinoma treated at Peking Union Medical College Hospital since January 1, 2015. Cervical neuroendocrine carcinoma is a rare and highly aggressive cervical cancer with no standard treatment. The study will analyze the tumor's genes, RNA, proteins, and immune environment to better understand its molecular features, identify molecular subtypes, find markers related to survival and immunotherapy, and build a prognostic prediction model. No new patients will be enrolled, and no additional tests or treatments will be given. About 80-120 patients are expected to be included. Results may help improve future diagnosis and personalized treatment for this rare cancer.
interventions: Multi-omics profiling of archived tumor tissue (observational)
primary_outcomes: Genomic Alteration Landscape
Transcriptomic Expression Profile
title: Multi-omics Study of Cervical Neuroendocrine Carcinoma

brief_summary:
This study investigates inflammation in the blood vessels of people with coronary artery disease (CAD) or a recent myocardial infarction. Inflammation plays an important role in the development and progression of atherosclerosis, but there is currently no established clinical imaging method for detecting inflammation in atherosclerotic plaques throughout the body.

The study uses a new PET imaging tracer called 18F-AlF-NOTA-Folate. The tracer is designed to bind to folate receptor beta (FR-β), a marker found on activated macrophages, which are immune cells involved in inflammation. The aim is to determine whether PET imaging with this tracer can detect and measure inflammation in atherosclerotic plaques.

Approximately 90 patients will participate. One group will include patients with suspected or stable coronary artery disease who are undergoing coronary CT angiography and PET imaging as part of their clinical assessment. A second, smaller group will include patients who have recently had a myocardial infarction.

Participants will undergo PET and CT imaging and provide blood samples. The imaging will examine the coronary arteries and other major arteries, including the carotid arteries, aorta and iliac arteries. The study will also investigate blood flow in the heart and other organs and examine the relationship between vascular inflammation, atherosclerotic plaque characteristics and markers of inflammation in the blood.

The study is not testing a treatment for coronary artery disease. The folate tracer is administered only for imaging purposes. Participants will be followed through hospital and registry records for up to five years to investigate whether imaging findings are associated with later cardiovascular events.

The study may provide new information about how inflammation is distributed in atherosclerosis and whether FR-β-targeted PET imaging could be useful for detecting and studying vascular inflammation in patients with cardiovascular disease.
primary_outcomes: Coronary 18F-AlF-NOTA-Folate uptake measured by a target-to-background ratio
18F-AlF-NOTA-Folate uptake in extracardiac arteries measured by TBR
title: Vascular Inflammation in Atherosclerosis - Whole Body Molecular PET/CT Imaging Using Folate Receptor β

brief_summary: This prospective, randomized, single-center study will compare sevoflurane inhalational anesthesia with propofol intravenous anesthesia in patients undergoing intracardiac echocardiography-guided radiofrequency catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation. Eligible participants will be randomly assigned to one of two general anesthesia groups. In the sevoflurane group, anesthesia will be maintained with sevoflurane, while in the propofol group, anesthesia will be maintained with propofol administered using target-controlled infusion. In both groups, anesthesia depth will be adjusted to maintain a Bispectral Index value between 40 and 60. The study will evaluate acute procedural success and atrial arrhythmia recurrence at 6 months. Additional outcomes will include mapping time, ablation time, total procedure time, hemodynamic instability, recovery score, and procedural complications.
primary_outcomes: Atrial Tachyarrhythmia Recurrence at 6 Months
title: Sevoflurane Versus Propofol Anesthesia in Intracardiac Echocardiography-Guided Atrial Fibrillation Ablation

brief_summary: Health literacy is critical for patient safety, quality of care, and long-term health outcomes, yet health professionals often lack the support, time, and tools to deliver health literacy-sensitive care (health literacy sensitivity is the knowledge, skills, and attitudes health professionals require to effectively meet patients' health literacy needs). Building on a successful feasibility study showing that a targeted intervention can enhance health literacy sensitivity and teamwork without harming mental or occupational well-being. The Health Literacy for Healthier Minds study will build on these positive results and test a scalable, multi-component intervention in four Norwegian hospitals. The study aims to strengthen health professionals' health literacy sensitivity, safeguard their mental and occupational well-being, and explore patients' experiences with health literacy-sensitive care.
interventions: The Health Literacy for Healthier Mind study
primary_outcomes: Health literacy sensitivity
title: The Health Literacy for Healthier Mind Study

brief_summary:
Addiction is a psychiatric disorder associated with craving, an unwanted, intense and persistent desire to use the substance/addictive behavior, leading to frequent relapses. Craving is fluctuating, influenced by internal factors or environmental context, and can be evaluated only by self-report which can be burdensome. It has been shown that craving predicts relapse, making it a major treatment target in addiction. Identify biomarkers of craving could enable to detect craving in a passive way (without major effort from individuals to report it) and would be a major improvement. The goal of this observational study is to explore if voice could be a biomarker of craving in adults with substance or behavioral addictions. The main question it aims to answer is:

• Is there voice features associated with craving episodes in addiction ? Participants will undergo a cue-reactivity protocol with different voice tasks, and then answer Ecological Momentary Assessment (EMA) questionnaires on smartphone, with some of the questionnaires recorded out loud with the smartphone's microphone.
primary_outcomes: Vocal acoustic features during the laboratory cue-reactivity protocol
Vocal acoustic features during daily life
title: Vocal Biomarkers of Craving

brief_summary:
Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) and high-grade B-cell lymphoma (HGBL) are aggressive lymphomas commonly treated with first-line immunochemotherapy. Some patients experience disease progression or relapse despite treatment. PET/CT is used to assess treatment response, but it may not identify small amounts of residual lymphoma.

Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) consists of tumor-derived DNA fragments detectable in blood. This prospective observational study will use PhasED-seq to assess plasma ctDNA before, during, and after first-line therapy in approximately 100 patients with newly diagnosed DLBCL or HGBL.

The primary objective is to evaluate the association between ctDNA status approximately 8 weeks after completion of first-line therapy and subsequent progression-free survival. Additional analyses will examine overall survival, earlier ctDNA findings, and baseline tumor molecular subtypes. PET/CT findings will provide complementary information for exploratory analyses. The findings may inform future studies of response-adapted treatment.
interventions: Standard-of-care first-line immunochemotherapy containing an anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody and an anthracycline, such as R-CHOP, Pola-R-CHP, or DA-EPOCH-R.
primary_outcomes: Progression-free survival following post-treatment ctDNA assessment
title: Prospective ctDNA Testing in Large B-Cell Lymphoma

brief_summary: The study aimed to compare the incidence of postoperative venous hypertension between side-to-side (STS) and end-to-side (ETS) brachiobasilic arteriovenous fistulae.

brief_summary: This cross-sectional observational study aims to examine the relationship between tibial nerve cross-sectional area at the tarsal tunnel and plantar fascia thickness, pressure pain threshold, foot posture, and functional status in individuals with chronic plantar fasciitis. Ultrasound measurements and clinical assessments will be used to explore whether tibial nerve morphology is associated with structural, pain-related, and functional findings. The findings may improve understanding of chronic plantar fasciitis and inform future prospective research.
lead_sponsor: Sultan Abdulhamid Han Training and Research Hospital, Istanbul, Turkey
primary_outcomes: Assessment of tibial nerve cross-sectional area with ultrasonographic evaluation
title: Tibial Nerve Size and Clinical Features in Chronic Plantar Fasciitis

brief_summary: This prospective observational study aims to compare frontal electroencephalographic (EEG) spectral dynamics between patients with obesity and normal weight undergoing general anesthesia. The primary objective is to evaluate whether changes in frontal alpha power around propofol-induced loss of consciousness differ between the two BMI groups. Secondary objectives include comparing changes in delta power, the alpha/delta power ratio, and frontal alpha asymmetry around loss of consciousness, as well as evaluating EEG spectral dynamics throughout the intraoperative period. Anesthetic management will be determined by the attending anesthesiologist according to routine clinical practice, without intervention by the study investigators.
primary_outcomes: Difference in Bilateral Spectral Edge Frequency Between BMI Groups During General Anesthesia
title: Frontal EEG Dynamics During Anesthesia in Patients With Obesity and Normal Weight

brief_summary:
Aim: The aim of this study was to examine the effects of the directed invention method on basic volleyball skills and reaction time.

Materials and Methods: A total of 40 university students with no previous volleyball training experience, enrolled at Bayburt University during the fall semester of the 2024-2025 academic year, participated in the study. Participants were divided into an experimental group (n = 20), which received the directed invention method combined with traditional volleyball training, and a control group (n = 20), which received traditional volleyball training alone. Each group consisted of 10 male and 10 female students. Both groups participated in an 8-week training program. A quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control-group design was used. Basic volleyball skills were assessed using a rating scale and direct observation, while reaction time was measured using the BlazePod system and wireless light disks. Descriptive statistics and normality tests were performed. The Mann-Whitney U test was used for between-group comparisons, and the Wilcoxon signed-rank test was used for within-group comparisons of non-normally distributed data. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 26.0.
interventions: Directed Invention Method + Traditional Volleyball Training
primary_outcomes: Basic Volleyball Skills Performance
title: THE EFFECT OF DIRECTED INVENTION METHOD STUDIES ON BASIC SKILLS AND REACTION TIME IN VOLLEYBALL

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if text messages can help adults with newly diagnosed high blood pressure (hypertension) bring their blood pressure under control. The study took place in primary care clinics in Bangladesh and Pakistan. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Do more participants who get text messages have their blood pressure under control after 6 months? Under control means a top number below 140 and a bottom number below 90.

Do text messages help participants take their blood pressure medicine as prescribed?

Researchers compared a text message program to usual care to see if the text messages work to lower blood pressure. They randomly assigned whole clinics, not individual people, to one of the two groups.

Participants:

Got text messages for 6 months, or got written health materials and usual care. Received daily messages for the first month and fewer after that, if in the text message group. The messages encouraged taking medicine, healthy habits, and checking blood pressure.

Had their blood pressure checked at 9 weeks and at 6 months.
primary_outcomes: Blood pressure control at 6 months
title: Text Message Support to Help Adults With Newly Diagnosed High Blood Pressure Control Their Blood Pressure in Primary Care Clinics in Germany and Pakistan

brief_summary: Dysphagia and thirst are common in the early period after thyroidectomy and negatively affect patient comfort. This study aims to evaluate the effect of cold water spray on dysphagia, pain during swallowing, and thirst after thyroid surgery. In this randomized controlled trial, patients will be divided into two groups. Patients in the experimental group (n=54) will receive +4 °C cold water sprayed into the mouth once every hour for 6 hours postoperatively, while the control group (n=54) will receive routine care. In both groups, data will be collected hourly for 6 hours.
lead_sponsor: Saglik Bilimleri Universitesi Gulhane Tip Fakultesi
primary_outcomes: Swallowing Difficulty Severity
Pain During Swallowing
Thirst Intensity
Dry Mouth Severity
