brief_summary:
Aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase deficiency (AADC-D) is a rare genetic disorder that affects the production of neurotransmitters in the brain and can cause severe neurological and developmental problems. Early diagnosis may allow affected children to be referred promptly for specialist care and evaluation for available treatments, including gene therapy.

The purpose of this study is to develop a newborn screening protocol for AADC-D in the neonatal population of Liguria, Italy, and to estimate the incidence of the disease in this population. The study will also establish reference values for 3-O-methyldopa (3-OMD), a biochemical marker used to identify newborns who may have AADC-D, and determine appropriate screening cut-off values.

Approximately 16,000 newborns born in participating hospitals in Liguria will be included in the study. After informed consent is obtained from their parents or legal caregivers, blood samples will be collected using dried blood spot cards as part of the existing regional newborn screening procedures.

The samples will be analyzed using tandem mass spectrometry to measure 3-OMD levels. Samples with positive screening results will be retested. If the result remains positive, genetic testing of the DDC gene will be performed to confirm the diagnosis.

The study will evaluate 3-OMD levels in the neonatal population, establish and periodically refine screening thresholds, and assess the preliminary performance of the screening method. The results are expected to support the development of a reliable newborn screening program for AADC-D in Liguria and facilitate the early identification of affected newborns.
primary_outcomes: Development of an Analytical and Post-Analytical Newborn Screening Protocol for Aromatic L-Amino Acid Decarboxylase Deficiency (AADC-D)
Incidence of Aromatic L-Amino Acid Decarboxylase Deficiency (AADC-D) in the Neonatal Population of Liguria, Italy
title: Newborn Screening and Early Diagnosis of AADC Deficiency in the Ligurian Population

brief_summary:
Research Objectives To compare the effectiveness of the education modules on the knowledge, attitude, and practice of male university staffs towards prostate cancer prevention behaviors by comparing the pre- and post-test of Iraqi male university staffs' knowledge, attitude, and practice.

Study population The research will proceed to be performed in the country of Iraq. Participants in the research will be male university staff members who are employed at Middle Technical University (MTU). This university contains 17 colleges and institutes, divided into five colleges and twelve institutes that are spread across four cities in Iraq.

Inclusion criteria

1. Males at risk are 40 years of age and over.
2. The male who educational level primary school and above.
3. The male who gives informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.
4. Men who did not receive any health education program about prostate cancer.

Exclusion criteria

1. The male staff outside middle technical university.
2. The male who has prostate cancer.
3. The male who is critically illness.
4. Withdrawal criteria include males who are unable or unwilling to comply with the study requirements, failure to attend the meeting schedules, and have substantial changes in health conditions, such as developing new medical conditions, having serious adverse events, or any other conditions that could impact the study results.

Study Design The study will be a Cluster Randomized Controlled Trial (Cluster RCT) study design among male university staff with a pre-test and post-test to evaluate the effectiveness of the intervention modules that will be used for the study in this phase. A control group will be chosen that has similar characteristics and functioning as the intervention group.

Sampling method The study will consist of selecting one college or institute out of 8 using a simple random sampling method, which will involve the classification of one college or institute for the intervention group and one for the control group. This will be done by utilizing a randomization process. The participants will be volunteers to participate in the study, and then the final selection of study participants will be determined by the specific inclusion criteria established for each group. The selection of participants will be contingent upon adherence to the predetermined sample size.
primary_outcomes: Effectiveness of a Novel Web Application Health Education Intervention in Enhancing Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices to Promote Prostate Cancer Prevention Behaviors among Male University Staff in Iraq

Effectiveness of a Novel Web Application Health Education Intervention in Enhancing Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices to Promote Prostate Cancer Prevention Behaviors among Male University Staff in Iraq
title: Developing and Validating Health Education Module for Prostate Cancer Prevention Behavior in Iraqi Male University Staff

brief_summary:
Venipuncture is one of the most frequent and distressing invasive procedures in paediatric care. Both immersive virtual reality (VR) and structured breathing-based active distraction have been proposed as effective non-pharmacological strategies to reduce procedural pain and anxiety. However, no randomised controlled trial has directly compared a structured breathing-based intervention with immersive VR and with the conventional technique.

The MOLIVeR trial is a single-centre, parallel three-arm randomised controlled trial (1:1:1 allocation) that compared the MOLI technique (a Spanish acronym for movilizacion, observacion, ludica e inmersion, matching the English Mobilisation, Observation, Ludic engagement and Immersion; a pinwheel-guided active-distraction breathing protocol), immersive VR (Meta Quest 3, Fruit Ninja VR) and the conventional technique in children aged 4-12 years requiring peripheral venous catheter insertion in a tertiary university hospital in Spain. The primary outcomes were pain intensity (Faces Pain Scale-Revised) and procedural anxiety (Groningen Distress Scale), assessed immediately after catheter insertion. Secondary outcomes were pre and post-procedure heart rate, first-attempt insertion success, procedure duration and adverse events. Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle.
interventions: Meta Quest 3 with Fruit Ninja VR
primary_outcomes: Procedural pain intensity
Procedural anxiety
title: MOLI Technique and Virtual Reality Versus Conventional Venipuncture for Pain and Anxiety in Children

brief_summary:
Presbyopia is a common age-related condition where the eye loses its ability to focus on nearby objects, typically from around age 45.

The standard correction is progressive addition lenses (PALs), but these have limitations: narrow viewing zones, peripheral distortion, and the need for unnatural head movements, which can affect comfort and safety.

Morrow has developed an electronically adjustable progressive lens (Morrow eProgressive) that dynamically adapts its optical zones.

This CE-marked device is already commercially available. This study compares its functional performance against standard PALs.

Approximately 50 adults (≥45 years) will participate at three sites (Belgium and Italy). Each participant wears both glasses types for three weeks each, in random order.

Researchers will measure head and eye movements during reading tasks, stair descent performance, and visual comfort via a questionnaire. Participants will also indicate their overall lens preference.
interventions: 3 weeks wearing of study device instead of their current wearing solution
primary_outcomes: Reduction in head gain
title: Evaluation of Functional Superiority of the Morrow eProgressive

brief_summary: While documented gender differences exist in drug efficacy and safety, men and women are often treated equally due to the absence of gender-specific clinical trials and approvals. Immune checkpoint blockade is used to enhance the immune system's ability to combat cancer cells and is approved for stage IV non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients with over 50% PD-L1 expression on tumor surfaces. However, uncertainty remains regarding whether immunotherapy alone or in combination with chemotherapy yields better results. Although both treatment strategies are approved, head-to-head evidence comparing these approaches is lacking. Large trials indicate that women derive less benefit from immunotherapy alone compared to men, while benefiting more from a combination therapy. However, women are often still treated with immunotherapy alone due to a lack of prospective clinical trial evidence supporting combined treatment's superiority. This world's first gender-specific trial aims to determine whether combined treatment is better than immunotherapy alone for female patients. All patients will be randomly assigned to one of the two treatment strategies, with the primary endpoint being the time until disease progression. Additional analyses will evaluate survival and quality of life differences. This investigator-initiated trial, has the potential to reshape clinical practice and improve outcomes for women with lung cancer worldwide.
primary_outcomes: Progression-free survival (PFS)
title: PD-1 Blockade Alone Versus in Combination With Chemotherapy as First Line Therapy in Females With Advanced NSCLC & PD-L1 Expression ≥50%

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to assess the impact of implementing a combination of heat education and school-based physical infrastructure interventions in reducing heat related illnesses and improving educational outcomes among primary school children aged 7-14 years in two climate-vulnerable districts of Bangladesh.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Whether different combinations of heat education and physical infrastructure interventions can reduce indoor classroom temperatures and heat-related illnesses and improve the health and mental well-being of primary school children.

Whether these interventions can improve educational outcomes among primary school children and provide cost-effective and scalable solutions for heat mitigation in low-resource settings.

Researchers will compare different combinations of interventions, including: (1) heat education with solar reflective paint, (2) heat education with bamboo ceiling and polyethylene foam, and (3) heat education with both solar reflective paint and bamboo ceiling with polyethylene foam, to assess their relative cost-effectiveness.

The interventions will be implemented in BRAC Education Programme-run primary schools in Gaibandha and Kurigram districts. Children will be the primary participants of the study. Researchers will assess changes in classroom indoor temperature, heat-related health outcomes and mental well-being among children, as well as their school attendance and academic performance. The study will also explore potential scalability of the interventions in similar settings.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Heat Rash
Incidence of Heat Cramps
Incidence of Heat Exhaustion
Incidence of Heat stress
Incidence of Heat Anxiety
title: Testing Interventions to Mitigate the Health Impact of Heatwaves on Primary School Children in Climate-vulnerable Districts of Bangladesh.

brief_summary:
This study aims to determine whether repairing the trochanteric bursa during hip hemiarthroplasty reduces lateral hip pain after surgery in patients aged 65 years and older with femoral neck fractures.

The trochanteric bursa is a soft tissue structure located over the greater trochanter of the femur. During surgery, this tissue may be opened to access the hip. At the end of the procedure, the bursa can either be repaired or left unrepaired.

A total of 102 patients will be randomly assigned to two groups. In one group, the bursa will be repaired using sutures. In the other group, it will be left unrepaired. All other aspects of surgical treatment and postoperative care will follow the same routine clinical approach.

The main outcome is lateral hip pain when lying on the operated side at six weeks after surgery, measured using a numerical pain scale from 0 (no pain) to 10 (worst imaginable pain).

Additional assessments will examine pain during daily activities, mobility, independence in daily living, and complications during the first three months after surgery.
primary_outcomes: Lateral Trochanteric Pain While Lying on the Operated Side at Week 6
title: Trochanteric Bursa Repair and Lateral Hip Pain After Hemiarthroplasty for Femoral Neck Fracture

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to assess the pharmacokinetic similarity of Biofilgragen, a filgrastim biosimilar, compared with EU-authorized Neupogen after single subcutaneous doses in healthy adult volunteers. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Are the maximum observed serum concentration (Cmax) and area under the serum concentration-time curve from time zero to infinity (AUC0-∞) of filgrastim similar between Biofilgragen and EU-authorized Neupogen?
* What is the time to reach maximum observed serum concentration (tmax) and terminal elimination half-life (t½) following administration of each product? Researchers will compare Biofilgragen and EU-authorized Neupogen to assess pharmacokinetic similarity.

Participants will:

* Receive a single 5 μg/kg subcutaneous dose of Biofilgragen and a single 5 μg/kg subcutaneous dose of EU-Neupogen in a randomized sequence during two treatment periods.
* Receive each study product after an overnight fast, with the two treatment periods separated by a minimum 32-day washout period.
* Provide blood samples at predefined time points after each dose to measure serum filgrastim concentrations and determine pharmacokinetic parameters.
* Undergo safety assessments and monitoring throughout the study, including the follow-up period.
primary_outcomes: Maximum observed serum filgrastim concentration (Cmax)
Time to reach maximum observed serum filgrastim concentration (tmax) (hours)
Area under the serum filgrastim concentration-time curve from time zero to infinity (AUC0-inf)
Terminal elimination half-life of serum filgrastim (t½) (hours)
title: A Study to Compare the PK and PD, Immunogenicity, Safety and Tolerability of Filgrastim Biosimilar and Neupogen Reference Product in Healthy Volunteers

brief_summary:
Food additives, in particular hydrocolloids (thickening, gelling and stabilising agents), are widely used in the food supply. Concerns about carrageenan have led the food industry to replace it with alternative hydrocolloids, yet no one has compared these different commercial additives with respect to their effects on health. Experimental studies indicate that hydrocolloids can interact with the intestinal barrier, gut microbiota and immune signalling, with possible implications for both the gut-liver and gut-brain axes, but how they compare in humans is unknown.

This study investigates how different food additives affect health in healthy adults. In an initial run-in period, all participants follow a standardised diet low in food additives to establish a common background diet. Participants are then randomised to receive foods containing different hydrocolloids - carrageenan and its commercial replacements - or a reference dietary fibre as comparator, on top of the shared background diet.

The study examines effects on the liver, gut microbiota and short-chain fatty acid production, as well as measures relevant to the gut-brain axis such as mood, gastrointestinal symptoms and sleep. By providing the first controlled human comparison of carrageenan and its replacements, the study addresses a timely public health and regulatory question: whether the reformulation already adopted by the food industry has any measurable consequences for gut, liver and brain health.
interventions: Xanthan and guar-gum baked in bread
primary_outcomes: Serum aspartate aminotransferase (AST)
title: AdHuman - Impact of Food Additives in Humans

brief_summary:
After a cardiac event like a heart attack or heart surgery, regular heart-healthy exercise is important to reduce the risk of further cardiac events and improve quality of life. That is why patients are offered exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation programmes. In these programmes, patients learn under medical supervision how to safely exercise after the cardiac event. The idea is that, after completion of the programme, patients should then independently continue to regularly exercise during their everyday lives.

But we know that many patients struggle to make heart-healthy exercise a habit during their everyday lives, even after completion of an exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation programme. Digital tools such as smartphone apps could be an option to help patients establish regular heart-healthy exercise in the long term.

aktvplan is a digital tool that has been developed in Austria specifically for this purpose. We are now conducting a study to find out whether aktivplan does in fact help patient to regularly exercise in the long term after an exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation programme.

aktivplan is an exercise scheduling app. At the end of the cardiac rehabilitation programme, the patient and the therapist discuss and agree on a suitable, personalised long-term exercise plan. The therapist then enters this exercise plan in the aktivplan app. The patient can view their personalised plan on the smartphone and check off completed exercise session. They also receive reminders and motivating messages to their smartphone. The therapist can see how many of the planned sessions the patient has completed. Should the patient struggle to complete the planned sessions, the therapist can contact the patient, discuss the reasons and possibly adapt the plan.

In this study, 68 patients will be included at several cardiac rehabilitation centres in Austria. They will be part of the study for 12 months after completing the cardiac rehabilitation programme. They will be randomly divided into two groups. "Randomly" means that the decision is by chance, like tossing a coin. The first group will receive aktivplan for six months after completing the cardiac rehabilitation programme, and then they will not have aktivplan for the remaining six months in the study. The second group will be opposite, so they will not have aktivplan for the first six months and then receive aktivplan for the second six months.

At the beginning, after six months and after 12 months, all patients will complete medical tests (exercise test, ultrasound of the heart, blood tests), measurements of their physical activity in everyday life (wearable sensor) and questionnaires (quality of life, self-confidence, anxiety). We will do statistical tests to compare how physically active and how physically fit the two study groups were at each of these time points. From this, we will be able to see whether aktivplan did in fact help these patients to regularly exercise in the long term.
primary_outcomes: Daily minutes of moderate to vigorous physical activity (MVPA) measured objectively by a validated wrist-worn wearable device (ActiGraph LEAP Pro) for accelerometry and heart rate measurements over a 14-day period
Maximal exercise capacity (Watts) measured by maximal cycle ergometry
title: Effectiveness of the "Aktivplan" Digital Intervention for Supporting Regular Heart-Healthy Physical Activity Following Phase II Cardiac Rehabilitation

brief_summary:
This research is a single-center, parallel-group, single-blind, randomized controlled experimental study planned to evaluate the effect of postoperative binaural beats (BB) application on the incidence of postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) and the need for antiemetics in patients undergoing elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy.

The research will be conducted in two phases. In the first phase, 30-minute binaural beats audio recordings containing alpha (10 Hz) and theta (6 Hz) frequencies will be developed to ensure standardization. In the second phase, the effect of the developed sound recordings on postoperative nausea and vomiting will be evaluated. The research will be conducted in the General Surgery Department of Kütahya City Hospital between January and September 2027. A total of 76 patients who meet the inclusion criteria for the study are planned to be randomized into intervention (n=38) and control (n=38) groups in a 1:1 ratio. Patients in the intervention group will listen to a binaural beats audio recording at approximately 60 dB sound level for 30 minutes through stereo headphones, starting 2 hours after being admitted to the surgical ward. In the control group, patients will listen to a placebo sound recording with similar acoustic properties but without binaural beats for the same duration and under the same environmental conditions. Both groups will receive standard postoperative care. The primary outcome measure of the study is the incidence of postoperative nausea and vomiting. The secondary outcome measures are the total score of the Postoperative Nausea and Vomiting Impact Scale, the clinically significant postoperative nausea and vomiting incidence rate, and the need for rescue antiemetics. Nausea-vomiting assessments will be conducted at postoperative 2nd, 6th, and 24th hours; the use of antiemetic drugs will be obtained from patient records. The obtained data will be analyzed using appropriate statistical methods and compared between groups.
primary_outcomes: Postoperative Nausea and Vomiting (PONV) Incidence
title: Binaural Beats and Postoperative Nausea and Vomiting in Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy

brief_summary:
The study aim is to evaluate the efficacy of the gastrocnemius plane block (GPB) in providing postoperative analgesia for patients undergoing foot and ankle surgery.

Objectives:

* To evaluate the duration of postoperative analgesia provided by the gastrocnemius plane block
* To assess postoperative opioid or rescue analgesic consumption within the first 24 hours after surgery
* To measure postoperative pain intensity at predefined time intervals using a validated pain scale (e.g., VAS).
* To assess the incidence of block-related complications, including motor weakness, vascular puncture, nerve injury, or local anesthetic systemic toxicity We hypothesize that GPB will result in lower postoperative pain scores and reduce opioid/rescue analgesic consumption compared with standard analgesic management after foot and ankle surgery.
interventions: GPB Group : This group will receive ultrasound-guided Gastrocnemius plane block with 30 mL bupivacaine (0.25%)
primary_outcomes: Time to first postoperative analgesic request
title: Efficacy of Gastrocnemius Plane Block for Foot and Ankle Surgery

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to evaluate the feasibility of a standardized locoregional anesthesia protocol for patients undergoing breast cancer surgery under procedural sedation or adjunctive hypnosis.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Can breast cancer surgery be successfully completed using this standardized anesthetic protocol without conversion to general anesthesia?
* Is this standardized protocol feasible to implement in routine clinical practice, based on patient acceptance, protocol adherence, anesthesia induction time, patient and surgeon satisfaction, perioperative complications, and reasons for conversion to general anesthesia?

Participants will:

* receive the standardized locoregional anesthesia protocol, combined with either procedural sedation or adjunctive hypnosis, as part of their routine clinical care;
* allow the research team to collect information from their medical records regarding the anesthesia and surgical procedure;
* complete a short satisfaction questionnaire before hospital discharge
interventions: Standardized locoregional anesthesia protocol for breast cancer surgery
primary_outcomes: Successful completion of surgery without conversion to general anesthesia
title: Feasibility of a Standardized Fascial Plane Block Protocol for Breast Cancer Surgery

brief_summary:
Post-bariatric hypoglycemia (PBH) is a complication of upper gastrointestinal surgery that causes recurrent episodes of low blood sugar after eating and can substantially impair quality of life. Currently, there are no approved therapies specifically indicated for PBH.

The purpose of this study is to better understand the physiological mechanisms underlying PBH and to evaluate three therapeutic approaches that may reduce hypoglycemia: dietary modification, treatment with a GLP-1 receptor agonist or dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist, and transoral outlet reduction (TORe). Participants will undergo detailed metabolic testing, including continuous glucose monitoring, mixed meal tolerance testing, and gastric emptying scintigraphy, to determine how these interventions affect gastric emptying, glucose regulation, insulin secretion, gut hormone responses, and hypoglycemia.
interventions: GLP-1 receptor agonist or Dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist
primary_outcomes: Postprandial Glucose Nadir Following Standardized Test Meals
Plasma Glucose Nadir During the Solid Mixed Meal Tolerance Test
Plasma Glucose Nadir During the Liquid Mixed Meal Tolerance Test
title: Dietary, Medication, and Endoscopic Interventions for Post-Bariatric Hypoglycemia

brief_summary: This randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial investigated the effects of combined antioxidant and anti-inflammatory supplementation on delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS) recovery in trained women. Sixty trained women (18-35 years) were randomized into four groups: G1 (Creatine + Omega-3), G2 (Creatine + Omega-3 + NAC), G3 (Creatine + Omega-3 + NAC + CoQ10), and G4 (Placebo). Outcomes included muscle pain pressure threshold, countermovement jump, handgrip strength, 30-meter sprint, bilateral dynamometry, infrared thermography, creatine kinase, and heart rate variability, assessed before and after an eccentric exercise protocol.
primary_outcomes: Countermovement Jump Height (CMJ)
Muscle Pain Pressure Threshold
30- Meter Sprint Time
Creatine Kinase (CK)
title: Antioxidant Supplementation and Muscle Recovery From DOMS in Trained Women

brief_summary:
Background:

Some brain or mental health conditions may be caused when a person s immune system attacks their own body. These are called immunologic neuropsychiatric disorders. In this natural history study, researchers want to see if they can find substances in the blood that can help them identify people with this kind of brain or mental illness. What they learn may help them find better ways to diagnose and treat these conditions in the future.

Objective:

To collect blood samples from people with a brain or mental illness that may be related to their immune system.

Eligibility:

People ages 1 month or older with a brain or mental illness that may be related to their immune system.

Design:

Participants will have 1 visit. This visit may be in person or by telehealth. They will answer a questionnaire about their health. They may have blood drawn for testing; this blood sample may also be taken at another medical facility and sent to the researchers.

Researchers will look at the participant s medical records and images over time. Researchers will also collect leftover blood or other tissue samples that are taken in the course of a participant s routine health care.

Participants may opt to have more visits. These visits will be every 3 to 12 months for up to 5 years. They will be asked about changes in their health since their last visit. They may opt to have blood drawn for research.
primary_outcomes: Identification of Recurrent Autoantibodies in Neuropsychiatric Subgroups
title: A Longitudinal Natural History Study of Immune Biomarkers in Neuropsychiatric Illness

brief_summary: Patients who are about to undergo cervical fusion surgery at Hospital for Special Surgery (HSS) are being asked to take part in this research study. The purpose of this study is to better understand the presence of bacteria in cervical spine surgery, using next-generation sequencing to identify bacteria in swab samples. A total of 76 participants will take part in this study at HSS.
lead_sponsor: Hospital for Special Surgery, New York
primary_outcomes: Metagenomic sequencing to assess bacterial presence
title: Assessing Microbiome in Primary Anterior Cervical Fusion Patients

brief_summary:
This prospective, single-center, three-group clinical study aims to evaluate the effects of binaural beat stimulation on pain and anxiety in adult patients undergoing flexible cystoscopy.

A total of 120 patients aged 18 to 80 years are planned to be included. Participants will be evaluated in three groups according to the auditory stimulation received during flexible cystoscopy: 5 Hz theta binaural beats (n = 40), 10 Hz alpha binaural beats (n = 40), and a control group without binaural beat stimulation (n = 40).

The primary outcome will be pain intensity during flexible cystoscopy, assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS). Secondary outcomes will include anxiety levels measured using the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory-State (STAI-S) before and after the procedure, as well as patient comfort and satisfaction.

The study aims to determine whether binaural beat stimulation may provide a simple, non-invasive approach to improving patient comfort during flexible cystoscopy.
primary_outcomes: Pain Intensity During Flexible Cystoscopy Assessed by VAS
title: Effects of Binaural Beats on Pain and Anxiety During Flexible Cystoscopy

The study will investigate whether this intervention improves \[primary clinical outcome\] compared with \[standard treatment or control group\]. Participants will undergo clinical assessment and follow-up according to the study protocol. The findings may provide additional evidence regarding the clinical effectiveness, safety, and potential benefits of this treatment.

brief_summary:
Acute appendicitis is one of the most common surgical emergencies in children. In complicated cases, where the appendix has perforated, become gangrenous, or caused peritonitis and purulent contamination, determining the optimal surgical approach remains an important clinical question. While laparoscopic appendectomy is widely used for uncomplicated cases, this study aims to evaluate its safety, clinical effectiveness, and postoperative outcomes compared with conventional open appendectomy in children with complicated appendicitis.

A total of 100 pediatric patients diagnosed with complicated acute appendicitis will participate in this prospective comparative study, divided into two groups:

* Group A: 50 patients undergoing laparoscopic appendectomy using a standard minimally invasive three-port technique.
* Group B: 50 patients undergoing conventional open appendectomy via a standard right lower-quadrant incision.

The primary goal is to compare the overall rate of postoperative complications between the two operative techniques. Researchers will also assess secondary outcomes, including operative time, intraoperative complications, conversion to open surgery, postoperative pain, time to resume oral feeding, duration of intravenous antibiotics, length of hospital stay, wound infections, intra-abdominal abscesses, bowel obstruction, readmissions, and reoperations. All participants will be evaluated during their hospital admission and followed up for 30 days postoperatively.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Participants With Postoperative Complications
title: Comparative Study Between Laparoscopic and Open Appendectomy of Complicated Appendicitis

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) plus immunotherapy compared with immunotherapy plus chemotherapy in patients with extensive transurethrally unresectable very-high-risk non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC).

Patients will be randomly assigned to receive either ADC plus immunotherapy or immunotherapy plus chemotherapy. The study will assess the effectiveness of these two treatment strategies in achieving complete response, maintaining disease control, and preserving the bladder, as well as their safety and tolerability.

The findings may help identify an effective bladder-preserving treatment strategy for patients with extensive very-high-risk NMIBC who cannot undergo complete transurethral resection.
primary_outcomes: Complete Response Rate of High-Risk Disease
title: Antibody-Drug Conjugate Plus Immunotherapy Versus Immunotherapy Plus Chemotherapy for Extensive Transurethrally Unresectable Very-High-Risk Non-Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer

brief_summary: This study will randomly assign overweight or obese patients with endometrial cancer undergoing fertility-sparing treatment to two groups. The intervention group will receive a comprehensive weight management program based on the DEAR principles of Diet, Exercise, Accompany, and Refresh, including intermittent fasting and structured aerobic exercise. The control group will receive balanced dietary guidance and self-directed exercise. Both groups will receive family and healthcare support, sleep monitoring, and stress-management support. By evaluating pathological complete response, body mass index, glucose and lipid metabolism, and serum AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) levels, this study aims to determine the effectiveness and safety of DEAR-based weight management in patients with endometrial cancer undergoing fertility-sparing treatment.
primary_outcomes: Pathological Complete Response Rate
title: Effect of Weight Management on AMPK Activation in the Adjunctive Treatment of Endometrial Cancer

brief_summary:
This study compares two surgical procedures for adults with painful, rigid progressive collapsing foot deformity, also known as rigid flatfoot, whose symptoms have persisted despite at least six months of nonsurgical treatment.

Both procedures fuse the subtalar joint, a joint below the ankle. One procedure also fuses the talonavicular joint, while the other fuses the naviculocuneiform joint. These joints are located at different points along the inner arch of the foot. Joint fusion joins bones together to improve foot alignment and stability. The procedure is selected according to where the foot's inner arch has collapsed.

The study evaluates changes in foot alignment on standing X-rays, foot and ankle function, physical function, and quality of life. It also compares operating time, bone healing, and complications. Both groups receive the same postoperative care and rehabilitation, with follow-up assessments during recovery and approximately one year after surgery.

The aim is to compare the outcomes of these two surgical approaches when each is selected according to the location of the deformity.
primary_outcomes: AOFAS
title: Subtalar & Talonavicular Arthrodesis v.s Subtalar & Naviculocuniform Arthrodesis for Progressive Collapsing Foot Deformity

brief_summary: This study tests whether a single dose of nicotine gum changes brain responses to sounds and the ability to detect target sounds in non-smoking adults with chronic tinnitus. In a double-blind, placebo-controlled, within-subject crossover design, each participant attends two sessions and receives a single 4 mg dose of nicotine polacrilex gum at one session and a flavor-matched placebo gum at the other, in random order. After gum administration, EEG is recorded at rest and during an active auditory oddball task. The primary measures are the P3 brain response (amplitude and latency) and oddball task accuracy and reaction time.
primary_outcomes: Auditory oddball P3 amplitude after administration (nicotine vs placebo)
Auditory oddball P3 latency after administration (nicotine vs placebo)
Auditory oddball target-detection accuracy after administration (nicotine vs placebo)
Auditory oddball reaction time after administration (nicotine vs placebo)
title: Acute Nicotine Gum and Auditory Brain Responses in Adults With Chronic Tinnitus

brief_summary: his study will evaluate whether tailored vaccine messaging improves vaccination-related outcomes among parents and caregivers of adolescents. Participants will complete a baseline electronic survey and will then be randomly assigned to receive either a tailored vaccine message based on insurance status or a standard vaccine message delivered by SMS text message. Approximately four weeks after receiving the intervention message, participants will complete a follow-up electronic survey assessing vaccination behaviors, vaccination intentions, vaccine confidence, perceived barriers to adolescent vaccination, and perceptions of the intervention message.
primary_outcomes: Change in vaccination intentions
Change in vaccine confidence
title: Tailored Vaccine Messaging for Parents/Caregivers of Adolescents

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized clinical trial is to determine whether vibrating foam rolling is more effective than non-vibrating foam rolling for improving ankle function and reducing muscle soreness after delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS) in physically active healthy adults.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

* Does vibrating foam rolling improve ankle dorsiflexion range of motion after DOMS?
* Does vibrating foam rolling improve dynamic balance after DOMS?
* Does vibrating foam rolling affect gastrocnemius muscle strength and passive muscle mechanical properties?
* Does vibrating foam rolling reduce pain and muscle soreness after DOMS?

Researchers will compare vibrating foam rolling with non-vibrating foam rolling applied to the opposite legs of the same participants to determine whether vibration provides additional benefits.

Participants will be physically active healthy adults. The study consists of two sessions separated by 48 hours. During the first session, participants will undergo baseline assessments of muscle properties, pain, ankle range of motion, dynamic balance, and gastrocnemius muscle strength. They will then perform a weighted heel-raise exercise designed to induce delayed onset muscle soreness in the gastrocnemius muscles.

Forty-eight hours later, participants who develop sufficient muscle soreness will repeat the assessments and receive foam rolling. One leg will be randomly assigned to vibrating foam rolling and the other leg to non-vibrating foam rolling. Each leg will receive three 1-minute foam rolling sets, with 30 seconds of rest between sets. Assessments will be repeated immediately after the foam rolling intervention.
primary_outcomes: Ankle Dorsiflexion Range of Motion
Dynamic Balance
title: Vibrating and Non-Vibrating Foam-Rolling on DOMS

brief_summary:
Diabetic symmetrical polyneuropathy (DSPN) is a common complication of diabetes that affects the nerves, especially in the legs and feet. It can cause pain, numbness, tingling, weakness, and loss of sensation. These problems can affect daily activities and quality of life. Loss of sensation can also increase the risk of foot wounds and problems with wound healing.

This study is comparing two treatments in people with type 2 diabetes and DSPN. The main purpose is to find out whether a combination of alpha-lipoic acid, vitamins B1, B6, B12, and vitamin E is providing greater improvement in neuropathy symptoms than vitamins B1, B6, and B12 alone. The study is also examining changes in wound healing.

About 100 participants are taking part at Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz (HCTM). Participants are being randomly assigned to one of two treatment groups. One group is receiving Bionerv E+, which contains alpha-lipoic acid, vitamins B1, B6, B12, and vitamin E. The other group is receiving a vitamin B-complex containing vitamins B1, B6, and B12. Both treatments are being taken daily for 12 weeks in addition to standard treatment for DSPN.

Researchers are assessing participants before and after treatment. These assessments are examining nerve problems in the lower limbs, pain, quality of life, and blood markers related to inflammation. For participants with diabetic foot ulcers, researchers are also assessing changes in the wounds.
interventions: Alpha-Lipoic Acid, Vitamin B1, Vitamin B6, Vitamin B12, Vitamin E
Vitamin B1, Vitamin B6, Vitamin B12
primary_outcomes: Change in Neuropathy Impairment Score-Lower Limb (NIS-LL)
Change in Neuropathic Pain Assessed by the Short Form McGill Pain Questionnaire (SF-MPQ)
Change in Health-Related Quality of Life Assessed by the Short Form-36 (SF-36)
title: Comparative Study of Combination Treatment of Bionerv E+ Versus Vitamin B Complex in Treatment of Diabetic Polyneuropathy in Type 2 Diabetic Patients and Its Effect on Wound Healing

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if tripterygium wilfordii added to prednisone can treat active IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD) in adults 45 to 80 years of age. Women in the study must be postmenopausal. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does adding tripterygium wilfordii to prednisone lower the chance that IgG4-RD comes back at 12 months compared with prednisone alone?
* Does the combination improve remission, disease activity scores, blood tests, quality of life, and remain acceptably safe? Researchers will compare prednisone alone to prednisone plus tripterygium glycoside tablets to see if the combination reduces relapse.

Participants will:

* Be assigned by chance to prednisone alone or prednisone plus tripterygium glycoside tablets 20 mg three times a day
* Start prednisone at 0.6 to 0.8 mg/kg per day and taper it off within 6 months
* Attend clinic visits at the start of the study and at 1, 3, 6, 9, and 12 months for exams, blood tests, disease scores, and imaging when needed
* Report symptoms and any side effects during the 12-month follow-up
primary_outcomes: Relapse rate
title: Tripterygium Wilfordii Plus Prednisone for Active IgG4-Related Disease

brief_summary: Magnetically controlled capsule endoscopy (MCE) is a noninvasive alternative to conventional gastroscopy with comparable diagnostic accuracy. However, mucus adherence to the capsule lens during examination can severely impair visualization, and MCE lacks an irrigation mechanism for lens cleaning. Current guidelines provide no intra-procedural recommendations for managing lens soiling. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of sodium bicarbonate solution in improving MCE lens cleanliness during gastric examination.
primary_outcomes: The proportion of study participants with a baseline lens cleanliness score ≤2 who achieved good or excellent lens cleanliness (cleanliness score ≥3) at the cardia after cleansing with sodium bicarbonate solution, defined as the cleansing success rate.
title: Sodium Bicarbonate Solution Enhances Lens Cleanliness in Magnetically Controlled Capsule Endoscopy

brief_summary: Locally advanced colon cancer, particularly T4 disease or colon cancer with bulky nodes, carries a poor prognosis and limited efficacy with neoadjuvant chemotherapy. In our previous small-sample phase II study, PD-1 inhibitor plus CAPOX chemotherapy combined with short-course radiotherapy yielded a marked improvement in the pCR rate compared with neoadjuvant CAPOX alone, though survival outcomes remain under follow-up. This prospective, multicentre, randomised, three-arm phase III study enrolls 480 patients with pMMR/MSS locally advanced high-risk colon cancer. Participants are randomised in a 2:2:1 ratio to three arms: short-course radiotherapy combined with chemotherapy and PD-1 inhibitor (25 Gy in 5 fractions of radiotherapy, followed by 4 cycles of CAPOX plus the PD-1 inhibitor serplulimab); chemotherapy plus PD-1 inhibitor (4 cycles of CAPOX combined with serplulimab); and chemotherapy alone (4 cycles of CAPOX). The primary endpoint is the 3-year event-free survival (EFS) rate. Secondary endpoints include the pCR rate, 5-year overall survival rate (5y OS), R0 resection rate, toxicity, surgical complications and quality of life.
primary_outcomes: 3-year event-free survival
title: Chemotherapy Combined With or Without Short-Course Radiotherapy Versus Chemotherapy Alone as Neoadjuvant Therapy for High-Risk Locally Advanced Colon Cancer With pMMR/MSS

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the effects of ultrasound-guided versus blind greater occipital nerve block (GONB), with or without Dexmedetomidine as an adjuvant, in pediatric patients undergoing posterior fossa tumor excision under general anesthesia.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does ultrasound-guided GONB improve hemodynamic stability compared with the blind technique?
* Does adding dexmedetomidine to GONB affect intraoperative and postoperative opioid consumption, postoperative pain control, and the time to first rescue analgesia?

Researchers will compare four groups to evaluate the effects of the nerve block technique and the addition of dexmedetomidine:

Group A: Blind GONB using 0.25% bupivacaine. Group B: Blind GONB using 0.25% bupivacaine with dexmedetomidine (1 μg/kg). Group C: Ultrasound-guided GONB using 0.25% bupivacaine. Group D: Ultrasound-guided GONB using 0.25% bupivacaine with dexmedetomidine (1 μg/kg).

Participants will be pediatric patients scheduled for elective posterior fossa tumor excision at Children's Cancer Hospital Egypt (CCHE 57357). They will be randomly assigned to one of the four groups and will receive standardized general anesthesia and bilateral GONB according to their assigned group. Intraoperative heart rate and blood pressure, intraoperative and postoperative opioid consumption, and time to first postoperative rescue analgesia will be assessed.
primary_outcomes: mean arterial pressure (MAP)
title: Dexmedetomidine Use for Greater Occipital Nerve Block in Pediatric Posterior Fossa Tumor Surgery.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether a single foot reflexology session reduces anxiety in pregnant women who are hospitalized in a high-risk pregnancy unit because of maternal or fetal complications.

The main question it aims to answer is: Do women who receive a 30-minute reflexology session have a greater reduction in state anxiety than women who have a 30-minute quiet rest?

Researchers will also compare the two groups on self-rated anxiety (visual analog scale), blood pressure, heart rate, and satisfaction.

Participants will:

* Complete anxiety questionnaires and have their blood pressure and heart rate measured
* Be randomly assigned to either a 30-minute foot reflexology session given by a certified reflexologist, or a 30-minute rest period in a quiet environment (standard care)
* Repeat the questionnaires and measurements immediately afterwards and rate their satisfaction
primary_outcomes: Change in State Anxiety (STAI-S) Score
title: Foot Reflexology for Anxiety in Women Hospitalized With High-Risk Pregnancy

brief_summary:
This prospective clinical study aims to investigate whether combining upper blepharoplasty with limited release of the lateral brow-retaining ligaments improves the long-term effectiveness of barbed thread brow suspension.

Lateral eyebrow drooping can contribute to an aged or tired appearance around the eyes. Although thread-based brow lifting can improve eyebrow position, the lifting effect may decrease over time. The researchers aim to determine whether releasing the tissue attachments that restrict eyebrow movement can help maintain the lifting effect.

The study plans to enroll 90 adults aged 20-70 years, divided into three groups of approximately 30 participants each:

1. Standard upper blepharoplasty alone.
2. Standard barbed thread brow suspension alone.
3. Upper blepharoplasty combined with lateral retaining ligament release and barbed thread brow suspension.

Treatment selection will be based on each participant's anatomical characteristics and clinical indications, without random assignment.

Participants will be evaluated before surgery and at 1 week and 1, 3, 6, and 12 months after surgery. Standardized photographs will be analyzed to measure changes in lateral eyebrow height. Eyebrow symmetry, complications, adverse events, and the need for revision surgery will also be assessed.

The study aims to determine whether the combined surgical approach provides more durable lateral brow elevation without increasing postoperative complications.
primary_outcomes: Change in Lateral Brow Height From Baseline to 12 Months
title: Enhancing the Durability of Thread-Assisted Brow Suspension Through Upper Blepharoplasty-Assisted Ligament Release

brief_summary: This study aims to evaluate the safety and efficacy of Ivonescimab alone or in combination with Cadonilimab or Ipilimumab in the treatment of advanced clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC).
primary_outcomes: Objective Response Rate (ORR)
Adverse Events (AEs)
title: A Clinical Study of Ivonescimab in Combination With Cadonilimab or Ipilimumab for Advanced Renal Cancer

brief_summary:
The goal of this pilot randomized controlled trial is to learn whether a family-centered early intervention program, delivered remotely to parents and carried out at home, can support the development of infants who were treated in a neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) and are at mild-to-moderate developmental risk (for example, due to preterm birth or low birth weight). The study will also look at whether the program helps parents' stress and well-being.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does the remote family-centered early intervention program improve infants' motor, cognitive, language, and neurological development compared with standard care? Does the program reduce parental stress and anxiety and improve parents' perception of family-centered care?

Researchers will compare an intervention group with a control group receiving standard information and routine follow-up, to see whether the program leads to better infant and parent outcomes. The study will include 36 infants (18 per group) with a corrected age of 6 to 10 months.

Participants in the intervention group will:

Attend weekly online sessions with the research team for 10 weeks Carry out a home-based developmental activity program with their infant Share short videos of home practice and receive feedback, with follow-up via messaging

Participants in the control group will receive standard information and routine follow-up.

Infant development will be assessed with the Bayley-III and SINDA, and parents will complete questionnaires on stress, anxiety, and family-centered care. Assessors will be blinded to group assignment.
conditions: Neurodevelopment in Mild-to-Moderate Risk Infants After NICU Discharge
primary_outcomes: Change in Bayley Motor Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Third Edition (Bayley-III) Composite Scores
title: Effect of a Telerehabilitation-Supported, Family-Centered Early Intervention Program on Neurodevelopmental and Parental Outcomes in Infants at Mild-to-Moderate Risk

brief_summary: This study will compare the clinical outcomes of a 1-month dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) strategy with a standard 6-month DAPT strategy in patients undergoing successful drug-coated balloon-only percutaneous coronary intervention (DCB-only PCI). The study will evaluate net adverse clinical events (NACE) at 12 months to assess whether short-term 1-month DAPT is non-inferior to 6-month DAPT. The study is a prospective, randomized, open-label, blinded-endpoint, multicenter trial.
primary_outcomes: NACE: at 12 Months
title: 1-Month Versus 6-Month Dual Antiplatelet Therapy After Successful Drug-Coated Balloon-Only Percutaneous Coronary Intervention

brief_summary: The purpose of our study is to investigate how dietary treatment with a modified ketogenic diet for patients with drug-resistant epilepsy affects patients' health-related quality of life and seizure frequency. We will also examine the diet's impact on cognitive functions, sleep, treatment side effects, microbiota metabolites, inflammation, and changes in the gut and oral bacterial flora, as well as the long-term aspects of this dietary treatment.
primary_outcomes: Health-related Quality of Life
Seizure Frequency
title: Modified Ketogenic Diet on Drug-Resistant Epilepsy in Adults - a Prospective Observational Study of Real-world Data

brief_summary:
Coronary artery bypass surgery is an important treatment method for severe coronary heart disease. Among them, minimally invasive bypass surgery, although having less trauma, requires a small incision on the left chest. During the operation, the ribs need to be opened and the muscles of the chest wall pulled, which is prone to causing intercostal nerve damage. Therefore, many patients still experience severe incision pain and chest wall pain after the surgery.

This study adopted the "Serratus Anterior Plane Block", which is a regional anesthesia technique. The doctor will inject the anesthetic drug into the gap near the pectoralis major muscle (a muscle located on the side of the chest) under ultrasound guidance. This technique can effectively block the nerves that transmit pain signals, thereby providing good analgesic effects for the anterior lateral chest wall and helping patients alleviate postoperative pain.
interventions: Ultrasound-guided Serratus Anterior Plane Block with Ropivacaine
Ultrasound-guided Serratus Anterior Plane Block with Normal Saline
primary_outcomes: Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15) score
title: Serratus Anterior Plane Block for Recovery After Minimally Invasive CABG

brief_summary:
Early postoperative delirium (POD) is a common and distressing neuropsychiatric complication frequently observed in elderly patients undergoing major surgical interventions, including radical and cytoreductive gynecologic oncological procedures (such as ovarian, cervical, and endometrial cancer surgeries). Delirium is associated with prolonged hospital and intensive care unit stays, functional decline, elevated healthcare expenditures, and increased perioperative morbidity.

The pathogenesis of postoperative delirium is multifactorial, involving baseline patient vulnerability and intraoperative triggering factors. Malnutrition and systemic inflammation are recognized as critical predisposing factors that disrupt blood-brain barrier integrity and trigger neuroinflammatory cascades. The Controlling Nutritional Status (CONUT) score and the Naples Prognostic Score (NPS) are objective scoring systems combining nutritional biomarkers (serum albumin, total cholesterol) and immune-inflammatory markers (absolute lymphocyte count, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, and lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio). Concurrently, intraoperative neuromonitoring (such as processed electroencephalography / bispectral index monitoring) provides continuous assessment of cerebral anesthetic depth and electrophysiological patterns like burst suppression, which have been implicated in acute cerebral dysfunction.

The objective of this prospective observational study is to evaluate the individual and combined predictive utility of preoperative immunonutritional indices (CONUT and Naples Prognostic Score) alongside intraoperative neuromonitoring parameters for the occurrence of early postoperative delirium in elderly patients undergoing elective gynecologic oncological surgery.
interventions: Preoperative Immunonutritional Scoring and Intraoperative Neuromonitoring
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Early Postoperative Delirium
title: Immunonutrition and Neuromonitoring for Postoperative Delirium in Gynecologic Oncology

brief_summary: During assisted mechanical ventilation, breathing results from the interaction between the patient and the ventilator. Optimal titration of pressure support is essential to maintain a balance between over-assistance and under-assistance. Excessive respiratory may lead to dyspnea and cause respiratory muscle fatigue, whereas excessive assistance promotes muscle atrophy and delays weaning. Although normal inspiratory effort values in healthy subjects are well defined, acceptable limits in critically ill patients remain unclear. Inspiratory effort is traditionally quantified by the pressure-time product (PTP), but its measurement is technically demanding. Simpler indices such as swings of esophageal pressure (δPes) and airway occlusion pressure at 100 ms (P0.1) are used more often, both with important limitations. Dyspnea, a frequent and distressing symptom among mechanically ventilated critically ill patients, may serve as a physiological marker of unacceptably high effort. This single-center prospective observational study conducted in the intensive care unit (ICU) of the University Hospital of Heraklion aims to (1) determine whether the ratio mean to maximal inspiratory pressure (Pmean/Pmax) correlates more strongly with dyspnea intensity than PTP, δPmus, P0.1 and (2) identify a Pmean/Pmax threshold predictive of clinically significant dyspnea. These findings are expected to define objective upper limits of acceptable inspiratory effort and guide ventilator titration to improve patient comfort and safety.
primary_outcomes: Association between Pmean/Pmax and dyspnea intensity
Comparative association of inspiratory-effort indices with dyspnea intensity
Discrimination of clinically significant dyspnea by Pmean/Pmax
title: Association of Inspiratory Effort With Dyspnea During Assisted Mechanical Ventilation in Critically Ill Patients

brief_summary:
The study involves two centers, only one of which recruits clinical cases. It is funded by the two participating centers according to their respective areas of expertise, in particular through research projects that will make use of sequencing services at IIT, as well as through IGG's institutional research funding and clinical diagnostic budget.

The study is therefore a single-center, translational, open-label cohort study.

Biological samples from patients and their parents selected to undergo whole-exome sequencing (WES) or whole-genome sequencing (WGS) will be collected and stored within the respective Clinical Units of the Giannina Gaslini Institute, specifically in the DNA Biobank and its associated repositories. Both blood sampling to obtain DNA samples that are not yet available and the use of existing DNA samples will be subject to the informed consent of the individuals concerned.

Appropriate DNA aliquots will be sent to IIT for sequencing after the samples have been pseudonymized using specific internal codes assigned by each IGG Clinical Unit. Any excess DNA remaining after completion of the sequencing procedures at IIT will be returned to the Gaslini Institute Biobank. Re-identification of the data associated with samples submitted for advanced genetic testing will only be possible by personnel designated by the heads of the respective Clinical Units who were responsible for sample collection. The same code, once linked to the corresponding Phenotips identifier, will be used to manage clinical and phenotypic data in the database to be established.

The genetic data obtained will be stored at the IGG-IIT Joint Genomics Lab in raw format (FASTQ) and made available to the IGG Bioinformatics Unit, which will process them into analysis-ready formats (BAM/CRAM/VCF) and compile the results into a report to be forwarded to the designated contacts in each respective clinical/genetics unit. At these units, the sample code will be decoded to enable communication of any resulting diagnosis to the referring clinicians and the family.
primary_outcomes: Establishment of a Clinical and Genetic Database of Patients with Undiagnosed Rare Genetic Diseases
title: Exome and Genome Sequencing of DNA Samples, as Required by Specific Research Projects and the Diagnostic Needs of the Gaslini Institute, to Be Performed Within the Framework of the "Joint Genomic Lab" Established Between IGG and IIT

brief_summary: The purpose of this phase I/II clinical trial is to test CARCIK-CD123/33 cells to treat patients with R/R AML/BPDCN, who have otherwise exhausted conventional treatment options. In particular, this study will assess the safety and feasibility of CARCIK-CD123/33 cells infusion in adults and children with R/R AML, ahead of scheduled alloHCT.
lead_sponsor: Fondazione Matilde Tettamanti Menotti De Marchi Onlus
primary_outcomes: Long term survival
title: CARCIK CD123/33 for Refractory/Relapsed AML and BPDCN in Children and Adults

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial was to learn whether adding dorsal penile nerve cryoneurolysis to medication and behavioral therapy helps men with lifelong premature ejaculation. Cryoneurolysis is a treatment that uses cold to temporarily reduce nerve signals. The study also looked at the safety of this treatment.

The main questions were:

Does adding cryoneurolysis make the time from vaginal penetration to ejaculation longer after 3 months? Does adding cryoneurolysis improve premature ejaculation symptoms and satisfaction without worsening erectile function? What side effects occur after cryoneurolysis?

Researchers compared cryoneurolysis plus medication and behavioral therapy with the same medication and behavioral therapy without cryoneurolysis.

Participants:

Took sertraline and tadalafil once daily for 3 months. Received education about behavioral techniques for better ejaculation control. Were randomly assigned either to receive one cryoneurolysis procedure or to receive no cryoneurolysis procedure.

Used a stopwatch to record the time from vaginal penetration to ejaculation and completed questionnaires during follow-up.
primary_outcomes: Change in Intravaginal Ejaculatory Latency Time From Baseline to 3 Months
title: Dorsal Penile Nerve Cryoneurolysis for Lifelong PE

brief_summary:
Breast cancer treatments are associated with frequent and sometimes severe adverse effects that may significantly impair quality of life and lead to functional disability. Chronic pain and cognitive impairment are common treatment-related complications. However, no study has yet investigated the influence of cancer treatment-related cognitive impairment on chronic pain in this population.

Primary Objective:

To evaluate the influence of cognitive impairment, defined as a significant alteration in the Global Composite Score (GCS), measured 6 months (±1 week) after completion of chemotherapy, on chronic pain over a one-year period following inclusion. Chronic pain is defined as persistent pain intensity ≥4.

The GCS includes 8 measures derived from cognitive tests assessing long-term memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, verbal fluency (categorical and phonemic), nonverbal fluency, working memory, and phasic attention.

The primary endpoint is the comparison of the percentage of patients with chronic pain between patients with and without cognitive impairment at 6 months after chemotherapy completion (T3).

Secondary Objectives:

1. Compare the percentage of chronic pain in patients with and without cognitive impairment at T2 (±2 weeks after chemotherapy completion), based on persistent pain intensity ≥4/10 on the Brief Pain Inventory (BPI).
2. Compare chronic pain characteristics and pain-related disability between patients with and without cognitive impairment at T2 and T3, including etiology, incidence, severity, localization, and disability. Pain characteristics will be assessed using the BPI, McGill Pain Questionnaire, DN4, NPSI, and a body diagram.
3. Compare, at T2 and T3, cognitive test scores used to calculate the GCS in patients with chronic pain to determine whether impairment in specific cognitive functions has a greater influence on chronic pain.
4. Compare the percentage of chronic pain in patients with cognitive complaints versus those without cognitive complaints at T2 and T3. Cognitive complaints will be assessed using the FACT-Cog and WMQ questionnaires.
5. Evaluate the influence of cognitive impairment on pain coping strategies at T2 and T3 using the Coping Strategies Questionnaire (CSQ).
6. Evaluate the influence of cognitive impairment on fatigue, anxiety, depressive symptoms, and sleep disturbances in patients with and without chronic pain at T2 and T3. Fatigue will be assessed using the MFI, sleep disturbances using the PSQI, and anxiety/depressive symptoms using the HADS.

Assessments will be performed at the following time points:

T1: before chemotherapy, but after surgery T2: after completion of chemotherapy (± 2 weeks) T3: 6 months after completion of chemotherapy (± 1 week)
interventions: Evaluation of cognitive functions in patients with beast cancer
primary_outcomes: Prevalence of chronic pain in patients with and without cognitive disorders.
title: Impact of Cognitive Impairment on Chronic Pain in Breast Cancer

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if ThIA Suivi, a digital tool for remote monitoring of patients, can improve the care of adults with depression who are followed by a psychiatrist.

The main question it aims to answer is:

\* Does using ThIA Suivi in addition to usual psychiatric care increase the proportion of patients whose depression symptoms have clearly improved after 3 months, compared with usual care alone? (Improvement is measured with a questionnaire on depression symptoms, the PHQ-9, and is defined as a drop of at least 5 points from the starting score.)

Researchers will compare patients who use ThIA Suivi with patients who receive usual care only, to see if ThIA Suivi leads to a greater improvement in symptoms. The researchers' hypothesis is that patients using ThIA Suivi will do better. \[

Participants will:

* Continue to be followed by their psychiatrist as usual.
* Use ThIA Suivi or will receive usual care only
* Complete questionnaires about their symptoms at 3 months, 6 months and 12 months.
* Be followed for 12 months.

Why is this study needed? Depression is a common mental health condition. It causes lasting sadness, loss of interest in everyday activities, and low energy. About 280 million people worldwide live with depression. It affects daily life, work, and relationships, and it can come back: more than half of people who have one episode will have another.

Depression is often treated with antidepressant medication. However, after 8 weeks of treatment, only about 1 in 3 people fully recovers. Side effects can appear before the benefits, which can make it hard to keep taking the medication. Close follow-up after treatment starts is therefore important. In practice, the first follow-up visit often happens late (a median of 27 days after the prescription in France). In addition, psychiatrists are not evenly spread across France, and most first antidepressant prescriptions are written by general practitioners.

Digital tools may help patients and health professionals stay in contact between visits. In France, however, no remote monitoring tool for mental health is currently reimbursed by the national health insurance. ThIA Suivi was developed by ThIA Santé Mentale to fill this gap. It is meant to be used within a care pathway supervised by health professionals. The researchers hope that it will improve patients' care, help them stay on track with treatment, and reduce the risk of the depression coming back.
primary_outcomes: Number of Participants with A Reduction of 5 Points in PHQ-9 Score
title: Remote Medical Monitoring of Patients With Depression

brief_summary:
Abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB) is defined as "flow outside of normal volume, duration, regularity, or frequency". Acute AUB is excessive bleeding that requires immediate intervention to prevent further blood loss. Chronic AUB refers to irregularities in menstrual bleeding for most of the previous 6 months.

AUB can be frequent or infrequent, prolonged, irregular, or heavy. Heavy menstrual bleeding (HMB) is defined as "excessive menstrual blood loss which interferes with a woman's physical, social, emotional and/or material quality of life". Causes of AUB are classified as polyps, adenomyosis, leiomyomas (AUB-L), malignancy and premalignant conditions, coagulopathy, ovulatory disorders (AUB-O), endometrial disorders (AUB-E), iatrogenic, and 'not classified ' . AUB affects approximately one in four women between 30 and 50 years of age, with serious implications on woman's quality of life (QoL). Endometrial ablation (EA) is a uterus-preserving procedure that aims to destroy or remove the endometrial tissue in selected women who have no desire for future fertility. EA has become an alternative to hysterectomy in the treatment of AUB because it is less invasive and has a shorter recovery period. At present, many different techniques are available to remove the endometrial tissue. Resectoscopic endometrial ablation (REA) consists of targeted endometrial destruction under direct hysteroscopic visualization. REA techniques include endometrial laser ablation, transcervical resection of the endometrium, and rollerball endometrial ablation. Non-resectoscopic endometrial ablation (NREA) uses a variety of energy sources to non-selectively destroy the endometrial lining and include thermal balloon endometrial ablation, microwave endometrial ablation, hydrothermal ablation, bipolar radiofrequency endometrial ablation, endometrial cryotherapy, and more recently vapor endometrial ablation. NREA technologies require short surgical time and can also be performed in the outpatient setting. Vapor EA is one of the newest approaches in the field. In this context, the Aqua Therapeutics Thermal Therapy Vapor Ablation system (ATTTVAS; AQUA Therapeutics Inc.) is a novel system designed to ablate uterine tissue using vapor thermal therapy technology. The ATTTVAS is indicated to ablate the endometrial lining of the uterus in premenopausal women with abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB) due to benign causes for whom childbearing is complete. In this A Pre-Market, Pivotal, Interventional, Clinical Investigation to Evaluate the Performance and the Safety of the Aqua Therapeutics Thermal Therapy Vapor Ablation System (ATTTVAS) in premenopausal women with Abnormal Uterine Bleeding (AUB)
interventions: Aqua Therapeutics Thermal Therapy Vapor Ablation System (ATTTVAS)
primary_outcomes: To evaluate the performance of the Aqua Therapeutics Thermal Therapy Vapor Ablation System (ATTTVAS) by assessing the change in menstrual blood loss at End of Study (EOS) visit, as measured by the Pictorial Blood Loss Assessment Chart (PBAC) score.
title: A Clinical Study of the Aqua Therapeutics Thermal Therapy Vapor Ablation System in Premenopausal Women With Abnormal Uterine Bleeding

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized controlled feasibility study is to assess whether a balance training program that includes dual-task exercises is feasible in people with multiple sclerosis (MS). The study also aims to obtain preliminary data on the effects of the training on walking under dual-task conditions and on brain activity recorded with a wearable EEG. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Is the training feasible in terms of recruitment, retention, adherence, data completeness, and assessment burden?
* What are the preliminary effects of the training on dual-task costs during the Timed Up and Go test (TUG) and the 2-Minute Walk Test (2MWT), on prefrontal activation and mental workload during walking, and on clinical outcomes?

Researchers will compare participants who receive the training with participants who receive no additional rehabilitation during the study period.

Participants will:

* receive 14 in-hospital sessions of balance and dual-task training (60 minutes, 2 sessions per week, about 7 weeks) if allocated to the intervention group, or no new rehabilitation if allocated to the control group;
* perform a dual-task walking assessment (TUG, 2MWT, backward digit span) while wearing an 8-channel wearable EEG headset and 3 inertial sensors, before (T0) and after (T1) the study period;
* complete clinical scales and questionnaires on balance, gait, cognition, fatigue, mood, pain, and quality of life.
primary_outcomes: Retention rate
Adherence to the training
title: Dual-Task Balance Training in People With Multiple Sclerosis: a Randomized Feasibility Study

brief_summary:
A non-profit, translational, prospective and retrospective study.

Patients will be enrolled according to the procedures described in the protocol, and samples will be processed and analyzed as specified in the protocol.

Since constitutional bone marrow failure syndromes (CMF) are rare genetic disorders characterized by a variable and incompletely defined clinical phenotype, a partially unknown genetic etiology, and pathogenetic mechanisms that are only partly understood, we hypothesize that a number of patients currently diagnosed with idiopathic acquired aplastic anemia (AAA) or idiopathic single-lineage/multilineage bone marrow failure (BMF) may have been misdiagnosed and may actually have an underlying CMF.

Therefore, our primary objective is to identify CMF underlying BMF and vice versa, by defining well-characterized patient cohorts based on clinical and family history, clinical manifestations, and immunological findings; identifying disease-specific parameters and biomarkers; and providing disease-specific guidelines to facilitate early diagnosis and, consequently, enable timely and appropriate treatment.

In this context, the use of appropriate artificial intelligence (AI) tools is likely to improve the diagnostic accuracy of this approach.
primary_outcomes: Early Diagnosis and Molecular Characterization of CMF and AAA
title: Enhancing the Clinical Management of CMF Through a National Pediatric and Adult Network Based on Biological and Genetic Data

brief_summary:
Schizophrenia is a chronic mental disorder that affects the diagnosed individual and the family members involved in the care process from a biopsychosocial perspective. The course of the illness, the recurrence of symptoms, and the high level of care required can increase the burden on caregivers and make it difficult for them to express their emotions. Structured psychoeducation and cognitive-behavioral interventions have been reported to be beneficial for caregivers in managing these challenges.

The aim of this study is to develop an AI-supported psychoeducation program based on a cognitive-behavioral approach for caregivers of individuals diagnosed with schizophrenia and to evaluate the program's impact on caregiving burden and the level of emotional expression. The six-week program will cover topics such as the caregiver role and burden, schizophrenia, the thought-emotion-behavior cycle, recognizing and expressing emotions, effective communication, setting boundaries, seeking support, signs of relapse, and crisis planning. Content based on scientific literature will be evaluated by experts. Artificial intelligence will facilitate interaction with the content, participation in activities, the application of skills, and structured feedback. The system will not provide clinical assessments, diagnoses, or personalized treatment recommendations; participants will be referred to appropriate healthcare services in situations requiring professional evaluation.

The study will be conducted using a quasi-experimental design with pre-test and post-test control groups. A total of 88 caregivers will be recruited, with 44 assigned to the experimental group and 44 to the control group. The program will be administered to the experimental group, while the control group will receive routine care. Data will be collected using the Caregiver Descriptive Information Form, the Zarit Caregiver Burden Scale, and the Emotional Expression Scale. A Program Evaluation Form will also be used for the experimental group.

The program to be developed is expected to reduce the caregiving burden on caregivers and improve their ability to express emotions. It is anticipated that the findings will contribute to psychiatric nursing practice, the development of AI-supported psychoeducation programs, and the strengthening of psychosocial support provided to caregivers.
interventions: AI-Supported Cognitive Behavioral Approach-Based Psychoeducation Program
primary_outcomes: Change in Emotional Expressivity Assessed by the Emotional Expressivity Scale
Change in Caregiver Burden Assessed by the Zarit Burden Interview
title: AI-Supported CBT-Based Psychoeducation for Caregivers of Individuals With Schizophrenia

brief_summary: Neurogenic orthostatic hypotension is a disabling manifestation of synucleinopathies including Parkinson's disease, multiple system atrophy, dementia with Lewy bodies, and pure autonomic failure. It commonly coexists with supine hypertension and requires individualized management. An implanted thoracic epidural stimulation system improved blood-pressure regulation, standing, and walking in a patient with multiple system atrophy, providing a rationale for further feasibility evaluation. This study evaluates the feasibility, safety, and preliminary hemodynamic response of lower thoracic epidural spinal cord stimulation in participants with symptomatic neurogenic orthostatic hypotension. All participants undergo surgical percutaneous placement of a lower thoracic epidural spinal cord stimulation lead, followed by an externalized trial stimulation period generally lasting no more than 2 weeks. During this period, the acute hemodynamic effect of stimulation is evaluated with a within-participant randomized stimulation ON/OFF comparison during a standardized orthostatic challenge. Participants who meet predefined response and safety criteria receive permanent implantation of the compatible spinal cord stimulation system. After permanent implantation, follow-up occurs at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months to evaluate symptom improvement and safety.
interventions: Lower thoracic epidural spinal cord stimulation
primary_outcomes: Difference in lowest systolic blood pressure during standardized orthostatic challenge with stimulation ON versus OFF
title: Spinal Cord Stimulation for Neurogenic Orthostatic Hypotension

brief_summary:
This ambispective observational cohort study aims to evaluate the association between vericiguat treatment and incident atrial fibrillation in patients with chronic heart failure. Adult patients treated at Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital between November 2023 and December 2026 will be included, with data collected retrospectively before January 2025 and prospectively thereafter.

Patients will be classified according to vericiguat use during routine clinical care. The non-vericiguat group will include patients receiving contemporary guideline-directed medical therapy for chronic heart failure without vericiguat. Treatment decisions will be made by treating physicians rather than assigned by the study investigators.

The primary outcome is incident atrial fibrillation during follow-up, including atrial fibrillation, atrial flutter, and subclinical atrial fibrillation. Secondary outcomes include all-cause death and major adverse cardiovascular events.
primary_outcomes: New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation
title: Vericiguat Use and Incident Atrial Fibrillation in Chronic Heart Failure
