brief_summary: Antimicrobial-resistant and healthcare-associated pathogens are a global health threat. The goals of antimicrobial stewardship are to minimize unnecessary and inappropriate antimicrobial use as a means to combat antimicrobial resistance. The interdisciplinary Videoconference Antimicrobial Stewardship Team (VAST) was initially developed and tested as a telehealth teleconferencing training and mentoring program in 2 rural pilot sites, then was extended to 9 rural sites, using telehealth to connect clinicians at a rural VAMC to a geographically distant infectious disease expert. Qualitative interviews showed that participants valued VAST and it improved patient care. This project will expand the VAST to other VAMCs and assess the VASTs' impact on antimicrobial prescribing. This work will directly increase access to antimicrobial stewardship consultation at rural VA facilities, which are often underserved by infectious disease expertise.
lead_sponsor: VA Office of Research and Development
primary_outcomes: Days of Antibiotic Therapy (DOT) / 1000 Bed Days of Care (DOC)
title: VA Quality Enhancement Research Initiative (QUERI) CARRIAGE VAST

brief_summary: The study aims to investigate the combination of the IDH1R132H peptide vaccine and the dual IDH1/2 inhibitor vorasidenib in patients with recurrent and/or progressive astrocytoma, WHO grade 2,3 and 4. The trial will assess the safety, and immunogenicity of the combined treatment.
primary_outcomes: regime-limiting toxicity (RLT)

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to investigate the effects of a specialized Cardio-Metabolic Clinic (CMC) in people with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease. The CMC provides integrated and individualized diabetes and cardiovascular care aimed at optimizing medication, lifestyle, and management of related health conditions. Treatment recommendations are supported by a decision-support algorithm combining individual patient information with current clinical guidelines.

Echo-CT-ProtecT-2D comprises two parallel studies conducted within the same randomized study population:

Study 1 - EchoProtecT-2D focuses on cardiac function and heart failure phenotyping. The main questions are:

* Can treatment in the CMC improve heart function at rest and during physical activity compared with usual care?
* Can treatment in the CMC reduce systemic inflammation and improve physical function, symptoms, and quality of life?
* How common is previously unrecognized heart failure, particularly heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), in this high-risk population?

Study 2 - CT-ProtecT-2D focuses on coronary inflammation and atherosclerosis. The main questions are:

* Can treatment in the CMC reduce inflammation around the coronary arteries compared with usual care?
* Can treatment in the CMC reduce the burden of coronary atherosclerosis compared with usual care?
* Can treatment in the CMC lead to favorable changes in the composition and high-risk features of coronary atherosclerotic plaques compared with usual care?

Participants will be randomly assigned to either treatment in the CMC or usual care provided by their regular healthcare providers.

Participants will:

* Have an ultrasound examination of the heart (echocardiography) at rest and during physical activity at baseline and after 12 months
* Have a CT scan of the coronary arteries at baseline and after 12 months
* Provide blood and urine samples
* Complete questionnaires about symptoms and quality of life
* Complete a six-minute walk test to assess physical function
* If assigned to the CMC, attend additional clinic visits as needed to optimize treatment
conditions: Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFpEF
primary_outcomes: Change in resting E/e' from baseline to 12 months follow-up, comparing the intervention and usual-care groups, with dedicated analysis of the HFpEF subgroup.
Change in global mean pericoronary adipose tissue (PCAT) attenuation from baseline to 12 months compared between the intervention and usual-care groups.
title: Effects of a Specialized Diabetes and Heart Clinic and Detection of Unrecognized Heart Failure in People With Type 2 Diabetes and Cardiovascular Disease

brief_summary:
EASY-VEIN NT is a pilot, prospective, single-center, non-randomized clinical investigation evaluating the safety and feasibility of the application of non-thermal high-intensity focused ultrasound (NT-HIFU) for the treatment of varicose veins of the lower limbs using the device of Veinsound's company.

A total of 15 adult patients, regardless of gender, presenting with superficial venous disease classified as CEAP C2 to C3, will be enrolled in this clinical investigation.

All participants will receive a single treatment with the investigational device.

The investigational procedure consists of the application of non-thermal high-intensity focused ultrasound (NT-HIFU) along the target refluxing vein under ultrasound guidance.

Follow-up visits are scheduled at 8 days, 1 month, and 3 months after treatment to assess safety and preliminary efficacy. An additional early safety visit is performed at 3 days after treatment for the first enrolled participants only.

Safety and feasibility will be evaluated through assessment of device-related and procedure-related adverse events, up to 3 months after treatment.
interventions: Non-thermal HIFU application along the saphenous vein of one leg / 3-month follow-up
primary_outcomes: Per procedure and late adverse events (AE) related to the investigational medical device, up to 3 months after procedure
title: Pilot Study: Evaluation of the Safety of the Application of Non-thermal HIFU for Varicose Veins Treatment of the Lower Limbs

brief_summary:
This study is a prospective non randomized controlled trial evaluating the effect of ultrasound-guided platelet-rich plasma (PRP) injections on peripheral nerve regeneration.

Patients receiving PRP were compared with a control cohort managed conservatively without PRP.
primary_outcomes: Change in Muscle Strength Using the Medical Research Council (MRC) Scale
title: Effect of Ultrasound Guided PRP Injection on Post Trumatic Peripheral Nerve Regeneration.

brief_summary:
The study team is studying how delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) - the component of cannabis that is responsible for "getting people feeling high" - influences how people think about the behaviour of others and a variety of other experiences. The study team is investigating these processes in healthy adults. The study team uses computer-based tasks and questionnaires to understand how people make conclusions about other people's intentions under different circumstances.

In this study, the study team uses a placebo-controlled within-participant study design with three different conditions: (i) 1mg/ml THC administration, (ii) 2mg/ml THC administration, and (iii) placebo (Saline) administration, all via an intravenous IV. The study is within-participants, meaning that every participant will experience all three conditions. The study is double blind, meaning that neither the researcher nor the participant will know what condition they will be in on a given study visit. The sequence of conditions is balanced across participants.
primary_outcomes: Harmful intent attribution
title: An Investigation of Mechanisms That Underly Paranoia in Behaviour and Brain That Can Inform Clinical Diagnoses That Include Paranoid Symptoms.

brief_summary:
This is a multicenter, randomized, controlled clinical trial comparing two surgical techniques for the treatment of chronic ankle instability (CAI). CAI is a condition in which the outer ligaments of the ankle remain loose and the ankle continues to give way after repeated sprains, causing pain, swelling, and difficulty with sports and daily activities. About 30-40% of patients who sprain an ankle go on to develop CAI.

All patients in this study receive arthroscopic repair of the anterior talofibular ligament (ATFL) - the main ligament on the outside of the ankle - together with an Internal Brace, a high-strength suture tape that provides immediate mechanical reinforcement. In the experimental group, an absorbable type I collagen scaffold (REGENETEN) is additionally wrapped onto the repair to promote the regrowth of ligament-like tissue. Patients in the control group receive the Internal Brace repair alone.

Eligible patients are aged 18 to 65 with chronic lateral ankle instability that has not improved with standard non-surgical treatment and in whom the ATFL tissue is of poor quality or a previous repair has failed. Participants are randomly assigned 1:1 to one of the two groups, and treatment is assigned by a central computer-generated schedule stratified by study site. Both groups follow the same standardized surgical steps and the same post-operative rehabilitation program.

The main question is whether adding the collagen scaffold leads to better ankle function and stability 12 months after surgery. Patient-reported function, pain, return to sport, MRI evidence of ligament healing, and any complications will be followed for up to 24 months.
lead_sponsor: Second Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University, School of Medicine
primary_outcomes: Change from Baseline in Karlsson-Peterson Ankle Function Score at 12 Months
title: Collagen Scaffold Bioaugmentation for ATFL Repair in Chronic Ankle Instability

brief_summary:
This is a pragmatic, risk-stratified, individually randomized controlled trial testing whether personalised WhatsApp-based digital behavioural nudges can improve completion of cardiovascular preventive actions after community risk screening at NADI centres in Malaysia.

Adults attending participating NADI centres will be screened using the MyHeartRisk web-based cardiovascular risk assessment tool. All screened participants will receive their risk result, standard risk explanation and general heart-health education. Participants classified as high cardiovascular risk will also receive a referral letter advising healthcare provider review.

Participants classified as moderate or high cardiovascular risk will be randomized 1:1 to either a personalised digital nudge arm or a no-nudge control arm. The nudge arm will receive scheduled WhatsApp messages over 90 days, including action prompts, reminders, engagement check-ins and barrier-solving messages. The control arm will receive standard risk feedback and referral-letter generation where indicated, but no scheduled behavioural nudges.

The primary outcome is completion of a risk-appropriate cardiovascular preventive action within 90 days. For moderate-risk participants, this may include completion of blood pressure, glucose or lipid checks, medication review, or healthcare provider review. For high-risk participants, this is attendance at a healthcare provider after receiving the MyHeartRisk referral letter. Low-risk participants will receive standard feedback and may be followed descriptively, but they will not be randomized or included in the primary randomized analysis.
interventions: Personalised Digital Behavioural Nudges (NADI-MyHeartRisk Enhanced Pathway)
lead_sponsor: Cardiovascular Advancement and Research Excellence Institute
primary_outcomes: Number of Participants Completing a Risk-Appropriate Cardiovascular Preventive Action by Day 90
title: Digital Nudges to Improve Heart Health Actions After Community Screening in Malaysia (NADI-MyHeartRisk)

brief_summary:
This study will compare starting Ocrevus Zunovo soon after an active episode of relapsing multiple sclerosis (MS) with starting it later. Researchers want to learn whether starting treatment sooner reduces the number of MS relapses over 18 months. They will also study changes in immune cells, blood markers, disability, and MRI scans.

About 35 adults with relapsing MS will take part at Oklahoma Medical Research Foundation or Corewell Health West. One group will start Ocrevus Zunovo before leaving the clinic or hospital. The other group will start treatment later. Ocrevus Zunovo is given as an injection under the skin. Participants will have blood draws and follow-up visits for up to 18 months. Researchers will also review their medical records for relapses, steroid treatments, emergency department visits, and hospital stays.

About 10 adults without MS will provide blood samples to help researchers compare immune cell measurements.
primary_outcomes: Annualized Relapse Rate Over 18 Months.
title: Early Versus Delayed Start of Ocrevus Zunovo for Relapsing Multiple Sclerosis

brief_summary: A seasonal pattern in the on- and offset of depressive episodes in recurrent depressive disorder is prevalent at latitudes with large summer-winter differences in daylength. In Denmark we estimate that 10-12% of the population experience winter depression symptoms with functional impairment, and 1-2% of the population is expected to fulfil the ICD-11 criteria for a recurrent depression episode with a winter seasonal pattern (seasonal depression). First-line treatment of seasonal depression is light delivered by a light box with exposure for ½-1 hour each morning in the season. Based on the physical characteristics and physiological responses daylight should be just as effective as light from a light box. Therefore, in this study the aim is to investigate whether 30 minutes daily outside walks for 6 weeks has an antidepressant effect.
primary_outcomes: Structured Interview Guide for the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale - Seasonal Affective Disorder Self assessment version (SIGH-SAD-SA)
Sleep onset latency
title: Treating Seasonal Depression With Daylight

brief_summary: This study explored the exercise fear experience of patients with lower extremity arteriosclerosis obliterans. We conducted qualitative interviews and identified four core themes contributing to patients' fear of physical activity, including physical discomfort, negative psychological feelings, biased cognition, and inadequate social and medical support. The findings explained how exercise fear gradually develops and forms a vicious cycle of activity avoidance. Based on patients' real experience, we proposed a targeted exercise support framework. This research helps clinical staff better understand patients' inner barriers to exercise, carry out individualized psychological and rehabilitation interventions, improve patients' exercise adherence, and promote long-term disease rehabilitation.
lead_sponsor: The Fourth Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University School of Medicine
primary_outcomes: TSK（Tampa Scale for Kinesiophobia）
title: Exploring the Exercise Fear Experiences of Patients With Peripheral Arterial Disease: A Qualitative Study

brief_summary:
Total-type sudden sensorineural hearing loss (defined in this study as severe-to-profound sudden sensorineural hearing loss with pure-tone average (PTA) \>70 dB HL) represents one of the poorer-prognosis subtypes of sudden sensorineural hearing loss (SSNHL). It is characterized by severe or profound sensorineural hearing decline occurring within 72 hours, frequently accompanied by tinnitus, aural fullness, vertigo and other symptoms. Although glucocorticoid-based comprehensive therapy has been widely applied in clinical practice, overall prognosis remains unsatisfactory for patients with total-type SSNHL, with low hearing recovery rates. Long-term hearing loss impairs verbal communication, sound source localization and quality of life, and is also associated with anxiety, depression and cognitive decline. Some patients further require hearing rehabilitation with hearing aids or auditory implantation, imposing substantial psychological and economic burdens on individuals and families. Therefore, exploring safer and more innovative therapeutic strategies carries important clinical significance.

Extracellular vesicles (EVs) therapy is an emerging cell-free therapeutic technology. Previous pre-clinical studies have demonstrated that EVs can ameliorate inner-ear injury via anti-inflammatory, anti-oxidative-stress and neuroprotective effects, showing promising therapeutic potential in animal models of noise-induced and ototoxic drug-induced hearing loss. The investigators' prior research revealed that EV treatment effectively preserved hearing and alleviated cochlear damage in noise-deafened mice. Meanwhile, the investigators have completed a prospective, randomized exploratory clinical trial (NCT06707389). Its results indicated that intratympanic injection of extracellular vesicles (EVs) yielded favorable safety profiles in total-type SSNHL, without serious adverse events observed, and demonstrated a trend toward superior clinical benefits over conventional therapy in terms of hearing recovery and speech recognition improvement.

Based on the above evidence, the investigators intend to conduct a multicenter, prospective, superiority-design randomized controlled clinical trial enrolling 146 patients with total-type SSNHL. This study will systematically evaluate the efficacy and safety of intratympanic autologous circulating extracellular vesicles (C-EVs) combined with glucocorticoid therapy, so as to provide new evidence-based medical data and therapeutic options for total-type SSNHL.
lead_sponsor: Sun Yat-Sen Memorial Hospital of Sun Yat-Sen University
primary_outcomes: The proportion of subjects whose pure-tone average (PTA) hearing threshold improved by >10 dB from baseline at 1 month after treatment
title: Autologous Circulating Extracellular Vesicles for Total-Type Sudden Sensorineural Hearing Loss

brief_summary:
The goal of this study is to learn if Core Transformation, a guided coaching process, lowers psychological distress in adults. It will also look at well-being, daily functioning, and whether any changes last over time. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Do people who have two Core Transformation sessions have less psychological distress after their second session than people who are still waiting for their sessions?
* Do any changes last up to 12 months after the sessions?
* Do participants feel better about the issue they chose to work on?

Researchers will compare a group that has the sessions earlier with a group that has the same sessions about 2 weeks later (a waitlist group).

Participants will:

* Choose one moderate issue to work on
* Be placed by chance into an earlier-start group or a later-start group
* Have two one-on-one online video coaching sessions with a Core Transformation coach (a coach in training or a certified coach), about one week apart. Sessions are recorded.

Everyone in the study is offered the sessions.

Psychological distress: Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) total score

brief_summary: This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of photobiomodulation therapy (PBMT) as an adjunct to the pulmonary rehabilitation program on the functional capacity of patients with COPD. This is a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind clinical trial conducted with 20 patients from the outpatient clinic of the Integrated Cardiopulmonary and Metabolic Rehabilitation Service of Santa Casa de Porto Alegre. Patients will be allocated to the active PBMT group, receiving photobiomodulation treatment prior to the exercise protocol of the pulmonary rehabilitation program, in the respiratory and peripheral muscles, or the placebo group, which will receive the therapy application at the same points but without the therapeutic dose, prior to rehabilitation. Sixteen PBMT applications will be performed over eight weeks, with a frequency of twice a week. The exercises performed in the institution's pulmonary rehabilitation program by the patients will not be interfered with by the researchers. Evaluations will be carried out in three stages: immediately after recruitment, after 8 interventions, and after 16 interventions.

title: PBMT Associated With a Pulmonary Rehabilitation Program on the Functional Capacity of Patients With COPD

brief_summary:
Rural left-behind children (LBC) are children in rural China whose parents have migrated to cities for work. They often face emotional and social difficulties because of long-term separation from parents. This study examines whether structured group music therapy can help improve the social adaptation of left-behind children.

The study has two parts:

1. A survey of 3,445 rural students across six provinces and one municipality directly under the central government (including 1,210 left-behind children) to understand the relationship between personality traits and social adaptation.
2. A randomized controlled trial with 24 left-behind children aged 10-14 years. The intervention group receives eight weekly 90-minute group music therapy sessions led by a qualified music therapist; the control group receives no intervention.

Children in both groups are assessed at three time points: before the program, immediately after the program, and one month later. The main outcomes are changes in personality traits (psychoticism, extraversion, neuroticism, and dissimulation) and social adaptation (psychological superiority, psychological energy, interpersonal adaptability, and psychological resilience).

This study will provide evidence on whether group music therapy is a feasible and effective way to support the mental health and social adaptation of rural left-behind children.
primary_outcomes: Change in Personality Trait Scores
Change in Total Social Adaptation Score
title: Music Therapy for Character Development and Social Adaptation Among Rural Left-Behind Children

brief_summary:
This observational, cross-sectional study aims to compare erectile and ejaculatory function between men with a history of coronary revascularization and men without known coronary artery disease.

The study included 135 adult male participants, including 66 men who had previously undergone percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) or coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) and 69 men without known coronary artery disease.

Erectile function was evaluated using the Sexual Health Inventory for Men (SHIM), premature ejaculation symptoms using the Premature Ejaculation Diagnostic Tool (PEDT), and ejaculatory function using the Male Sexual Health Questionnaire-Ejaculatory Dysfunction (MSHQ-EjD). Self-reported ejaculation latency was also assessed.

The primary objective was to investigate the association between previous coronary revascularization and erectile function. Secondary objectives included comparing premature ejaculation symptoms, ejaculatory function, and ejaculation latency between the two groups.
primary_outcomes: Erectile Function Assessed by SHIM
title: Erectile and Ejaculatory Function Following Coronary Revascularization

Adults undergoing elective middle ear surgery under general anesthesia will receive the block before induction, either with bupivacaine alone or with bupivacaine plus dexmedetomidine. primary_outcomes: Duration of Analgesia
title: Dexmedetomidine as an Adjuvant to Greater Auricular Nerve Block in Middle Ear Surgeries

brief_summary:
Many older adults who need liver surgery (hepatectomy) are physically weak before their operation. This can make recovery harder and may lead to more complications after surgery. "Prehabilitation" is a program of exercise and nutrition support that takes place before surgery, with the goal of helping patients get stronger and better prepared.

This study is testing whether a preoperative prehabilitation program helps older adults recover better after liver surgery. We want to find out if it reduces complications and helps patients return to their normal activities sooner.

We are looking for adults aged 65 and older who are scheduled to have liver surgery. Participants will be assigned by chance to either the prehabilitation program or standard care before surgery. The prehabilitation program includes guided exercise and nutrition advice over several weeks before the operation.

If this program works, it could become a routine part of care for older adults preparing for liver surgery, helping them have safer operations and smoother recoveries.

brief_summary:
This study evaluates whether an artificial intelligence (AI) conversational agent called MINERVA (Medical Interface for Navigating the Emergency Room with Voice Assistance) can safely and feasibly gather medical histories from emergency department (ED) patients and produce accurate summaries. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Can an AI conversational agent gather and summarize patient histories in the emergency department?

Are the resulting summaries accurate? Do they capture essential clinical information?

Can an AI agent overseeing these conversations independently identify red-flag symptoms that may need time-sensitive clinical interventions?

Adult ED patients interact with MINERVA via either voice chat or typing on a keyboard. MINERVA asks them questions about their symptoms and generates a summary which the patients review for accuracy. MINERVA reviews the conversation for clinical red flags that suggest urgent evaluation is required. Participants fill out a survey providing feedback on their experience. The summary is not saved in the medical record and clinical care is not affected.

Physician reviewers will evaluate the safety, accuracy, and clinical value of the MINERVA interview transcripts and summaries using standardized rubrics, including whether MINERVA was correct in identifying red-flag symptoms that may need time-sensitive clinical interventions.
primary_outcomes: Safety Diagnoses

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) can change the gut microbiome and improve health outcomes in females with anorexia nervosa. FMT involves transferring microorganisms from the stool of a carefully screened healthy donor to the intestine of another person. In this study, FMT will be given as capsules that are swallowed by the participants.

The main questions the study aims to answer are:

* Does repeated treatment with FMT change the gut microbiome in females with anorexia nervosa?
* Does FMT improve symptoms and other health outcomes related to anorexia nervosa?
* How does FMT affect gastrointestinal function, including bowel habits and gut transit time in females with anorexia nervosa?
* What medical problems or side effects do the participants experience during the study?

Researchers will compare FMT capsules with placebo capsules to see whether FMT affects the gut microbiome, gastrointestinal function, and symptoms related to anorexia nervosa. Placebo capsules are similar to the FMT capsules but do not contain donor fecal material.

Participants will:

* Receive five weekly FMT treatments and five weekly placebo treatments
* Be randomly assigned to receive either FMT followed by placebo or placebo followed by FMT
* Attend four study visits for clinical assessments and follow-up
* Provide stool and blood samples at the study visits
* Complete questionnaires about eating disorder symptoms, gastrointestinal symptoms, and general health
* Provide information about bowel habits and other aspects of gastrointestinal function

Neither the participants nor the study staff will know which treatment is being given during each treatment period. The study will include females aged 15 years or older with anorexia nervosa.

The study will help researchers better understand the relationship between the gut microbiome and anorexia nervosa and whether changing the gut microbiome with FMT could potentially be a future treatment approach.
primary_outcomes: Change in Gut Microbiome Composition (T0-T1)
title: Fecal Microbiota Transplantation in Females With Anorexia Nervosa

brief_summary:
Temporomandibular disorders (TMDs) cause pain and dysfunction in the masticatory system, often managed with occlusal splint therapy. However, splint therapy alone may yield inconsistent results. Low-level laser therapy (LLLT) has been proposed as an adjunctive treatment to enhance pain relief and muscle function through photo biomodulation. Evidence comparing the efficacy of splint therapy alone versus its combination with LLLT remains limited. This study aims to evaluate, clinically and electromyographically.

The evidence for occlusal splints is mixed: some systematic reviews report possible short-term benefits for muscle pain but overall the evidence is inconclusive and of variable quality. Low-level laser therapy (LLLT) has been studied for TMD and orofacial pain with several systematic reviews and meta-analyses showing potential analgesic and anti-inflammatory effects, though study heterogeneity exists.

EMG will be used for measurement of muscle activity before and after occlusal splint and low level laser in patients with pain in TMJ.
primary_outcomes: Treatment of Tempromandibular joint Pain
title: Clinical and Electromyographic Assessment of Occlusal Splint Therapy

Assessing exposome components enables a better understanding of the complex interplay between the environment, lifestyle, and health status. This study aims to provide mechanistic insight into the impact of exposomic factors-such as climatic variations, lifestyle behaviors, and pollution-on NCDs.

The main question is: Do creatine kinase levels after exercise differ between people who receive active microcurrent therapy and those who receive a sham treatment?

Twenty participants will complete a standardized exercise session. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups: 10 will use an active microcurrent device, and 10 will use a sham device for the same period after exercise. The sham device looks and lights up like the active device but delivers no microcurrents.

Researchers will measure creatine kinase before exercise and 24 and 48 hours afterward, then compare how levels change in the two groups. Investigators will also measure blood lactate and perceived effort shortly after exercise, before either device is applied. Participants will report any difficulties using the device, discomfort, effects on sleep or rest, and unwanted effects.

The goal of this clinical trial is to investigate the role of estrogen and isoflavone supplementation in exercise-induced cellular signaling and cardiometabolic adaptations in premenopausal and postmenopausal women. The study will evaluate vascular function, mitochondrial function, acute and long-term exercise responsiveness, and menopause-related outcomes.

Approximately 180 adults with moderate-to-severe nasolabial folds will be randomly assigned to one of the two treatment groups. An independent evaluator who does not know the treatment assignment will assess changes in the nasolabial folds during follow-up. The main purpose of the study is to compare the effectiveness of the two procedures 7 months after treatment. This multicenter longitudinal observational cohort study aims to characterize objective disease-control trajectories, treatment adaptation, and long-term clinical outcomes among adults with ulcerative colitis receiving routine clinical care.

Longitudinal clinical information, laboratory biomarkers, endoscopic assessments, intestinal ultrasound when available, medication exposure, corticosteroid use, hospitalization, surgery, and other clinically relevant events will be integrated to reconstruct time-varying disease states.

The primary longitudinal construct is time under objective uncontrolled disease (TUOD), defined as the cumulative proportion of evaluable follow-up time during which objective evidence indicates inadequately controlled ulcerative colitis. Periods without sufficient information to determine objective inflammatory status will be classified separately as unknown or unobservable rather than assumed to represent disease control.

The study will also evaluate two prespecified treatment-strategy questions. First, among patients initiating advanced therapy, long-term outcomes will be compared according to the initial advanced-therapy strategy irrespective of subsequent treatment modification or switching. Second, among patients developing confirmed objective disease non-control during advanced therapy, outcomes associated with alternative treatment-adaptation strategies, including within-mechanism optimization and switching to an alternative therapeutic mechanism, will be evaluated.

The study is non-interventional. Treatment selection, treatment optimization, switching, diagnostic investigations, and follow-up are determined by treating physicians according to routine clinical practice and are not assigned by the study.

primary_outcomes: Time Under Objective Uncontrolled Disease
title: Objective Disease Control and Treatment Strategies in Ulcerative Colitis

brief_summary:
This is a prospective, multicenter phase II clinical study designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of ipilimumab N01 in combination with sintilimab in patients with MSI-H/dMMR gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma.

The study comprises two cohorts. Cohort 1 plans to enroll 19 treatment-naïve patients with resectable locally advanced (cT2-4N+M0) MSI-H/dMMR gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma as determined by imaging (contrast-enhanced CT or contrast-enhanced MRI), who will receive 4 cycles of neoadjuvant therapy with ipilimumab N01 (1 mg/kg IV, Q6W, D1, for a total of 2 doses) in combination with sintilimab (200 mg IV, Q3W, D1) (21 days per cycle), followed by radical D2 resection, and then 13 cycles of adjuvant sintilimab monotherapy postoperatively.

Cohort 2 plans to enroll 17 patients with initially unresectable MSI-H/dMMR gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma, who will receive conversion therapy with sintilimab in combination with ipilimumab N01, with MDT assessment of surgical feasibility every 2 cycles; those deemed operable will undergo surgical resection followed by adjuvant sintilimab monotherapy for up to 1 year postoperatively, while those deemed inoperable will continue treatment until PD or intolerable toxicity.
primary_outcomes: Pathological Complete Response (pCR) Rate (Cohort 1)
R0 Conversion Rate (Cohort 2)
title: A Phase II Study of Ipilimumab N01 Plus Sintilimab for MSI-H or dMMR Gastric and Gastroesophageal Junction Cancer

brief_summary:
This prospective, multicenter, randomized, controlled, noninferiority trial will compare local anesthesia with conscious sedation and general anesthesia in patients undergoing pulsed field ablation for paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.

A total of 390 participants aged 18 to 80 years will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to undergo pulsed field ablation under either local anesthesia with conscious sedation or general anesthesia. Both groups will receive pulmonary vein isolation using the same pulsed field ablation strategy.

The primary outcome is recurrence of an electrocardiographically documented atrial tachyarrhythmia after an 8-week post-ablation blanking period. Recurrence is defined as atrial fibrillation, atrial flutter, or atrial tachycardia lasting at least 30 seconds through 12 months after ablation.

The study will also compare the ability of each anesthesia strategy to support successful completion of the ablation procedure, anesthesia-related and ablation-related complications, procedural efficiency, patient-reported pain and anxiety, overall procedural experience, and direct medical costs.
lead_sponsor: China National Center for Cardiovascular Diseases
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Participants With Recurrence of Atrial Tachyarrhythmia After the Blanking Period
title: Conscious Sedation Versus General Anesthesia for Pulsed Field Ablation in Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation

brief_summary: The dimensional collapse of the alveolar ridge following tooth extraction represents a critical challenge for implant rehabilitation. This research proposes an alveolar ridge preservation (ARP) protocol based on the combination of a slow-resorbing alloplastic synthetic biomaterial and a polymer-based resorbable synthetic membrane. Through a digital workflow integrating cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) and intraoral scanning (Carestream 3800), volumetric changes in hard and soft tissues will be monitored. The study will compare baseline conditions with outcomes at 4 months of healing, analyzing whether the use of the membrane ensures adequate support for the gingival phenotype and minimizes buccal bone plate resorption.

brief_summary:
Study objectives: Our study aimed to assess the prevalence, characteristics, and treatment of patients with resistant hypertension (HTN) in Bulgarian hypertensive population.

Methods: We screened 4340 consecutive cardiovascular patients hospitalized in our clinic and identified 3762 with HTN. Of them, 128 fulfilled the current (2018) European Society of Cardiology and (2023) European Society of Hypertension criteria for resistant HTN and were included in our study. We matched these patients to 128 hospitalized patients with controlled HTN.
primary_outcomes: Treatment resistance
title: Prevalence, Clinical Characteristics and Treatment of Bulgarian Patients With Resistant Hypertension

brief_summary:
Chronic migraine is a disabling neurological condition that can significantly affect quality of life, emotional well-being, social participation, and daily functioning. Although anti-CGRP monoclonal antibodies have substantially improved migraine management for many patients, little is known about the psychological experiences and adjustment processes associated with these treatments.

This observational study aims to explore the psychological adaptation of adults with chronic migraine treated with anti-CGRP monoclonal antibodies. Participants will complete standardized questionnaires assessing migraine-related disability, headache impact, anxiety and depressive symptoms, quality of life, and treatment experiences at treatment initiation and after 12 months of follow-up. Psychological interviews will also be conducted to explore patients' perceptions, coping strategies, and lived experiences of treatment.

The study seeks to identify factors associated with positive or negative psychological adaptation to treatment and to better understand patients' emotional experiences throughout their care pathway. The findings may contribute to the development of tailored psychological support interventions for individuals living with chronic migraine.
primary_outcomes: Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS) total, anxiety, and depression scores
title: Psychological Support for Chronic Migraine Patients Treated With Anti-CGRP (Anti-Calcitonin Gene-Related Peptide ) Monoclonal Antibodies
